Sports.title: Spotlight: How Monaco GP boss used sand trucks to beat Ecclestone | Brief
Sports.content:
As president of the Automobile Club de Monaco, Michel Boeri has been responsible for securing the future of Formula 1’s most famous race for over 50 years.

Before Liberty Media took over F1, that meant dealing with Bernie Ecclestone. In the seventies, Ecclestone ran the Formula One Constuctors’ Association, which negotiated on behalf of teams (a majority of which were British) with race promoters.

According to Boeri, Ecclestone’s uncompromising tactics required a firm response, as in one case soon after he took over as ACM president in 1972.

“Ecclestone was British, and he was a businessman. I was a rookie,” Boeri told Nice-Matin. “On the eve of the race, he told me: ‘Since we can’t agree on the fee, we’re going on strike.’

“There was no paddock yet, and the teams were based in the Portier parking lot. I called the Spada company and had the exits blocked with sand trucks. Then I went to Ecclestone and told him: ‘You don’t want to race? Fine. Then you’re not getting out.’ That got negotiations moving immediately.”

Boeri’s tactics achieved the desired result – though he also had the police ready to intervene.

“Ecclestone was a man of his word,” he said. “So I went down to the British camp to sign an agreement. There were no lawyers. It was simply: ‘I promise to move the trucks, and you promise to race. Signed, with love.’

“Being very brave, I had still called the police commander beforehand to tell him the British were drunk and aggressive, and to intervene if things got out of hand.

“I handed the paper to Ecclestone, he signed it, and I dropped to one knee. They took it the wrong way and thought a fight was about to break out. Then the cavalry charged! [laughs] It was ridiculous, but we weren’t writing a manual on diplomacy. You went on instinct. You felt your way through it.”

Sports.title: Lindblad vs Lawson: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Liam Lawson has finally begun what looks like being his first complete season with the same team and the stability appears to be paying off.

Having spent most of last season at Racing Bulls, Lawson has been a regular in the points. He has helped put the team fifth in the standings, on course for what would be its strongest championship finish in any of its guises.

But newcomer Arvid Lindblad has acquitted himself extremely well and goes into the summer break having tapped a strong vein of form. He’s scored in each of the last six grands prix and out-qualified Lawson in the last three – by decent margins, too.

So while Lawson’s numbers look good at the moment, he can’t be complacent about the growing threat on the other side of the Racing Bulls garage. Max Verstappen has all the reasons he needs to jump ship at the top team and if Lawson has a realistic chance of returning he needs to ensure he is the obvious choice. That won’t be the case as long as Lindblad keeps out-qualifying him.

As is often the case at Red Bull’s junior team, there is also pressure from below. Red Bull’s Nikola Tsolov leading the Formula 2 standings in his rookie campaign and the team will surely already be thinking about when he will be ready for a shot at F1.

Sports.title: Verstappen vs Hadjar: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar began his first full season at Red Bull knowing that the last driver in the same position as him lasted just two rounds before being booted out.

That must have been a daunting prospect to contemplate, though it bears pointing out that the senior race team management has changed significantly at Red Bull since Liam Lawson was shown the door after his pair of starts for the team last year.

The more experienced Yuki Tsunoda took Lawson’s place and became the latest in a series of drivers whose reputations took a brutal battering from occupying the garage adjacent to Max Verstappen’s. Tsunoda mustered just 7.2% of Red Bull’s points while alongside Verstappen.

This is the context in which to assess Hadjar’s performance this year. His 8-2 deficit in qualifying is nothing to brag about but he has been much closer to Verstappen over a single flying lap than his predecessors.

Hadjar has done vastly better at collecting points, too, claiming 38% of Red Bull’s score so far. True, compared to Tsunoda he’s had the benefit of a wider field spread between Red Bull and the midfield, but even so he’s already taken more than twice as many points as Tsunoda managed over his 22-race stint at the team last year.

He has achieved this alongside a formidable talent in a car which both drivers have termed “undriveable” on occasions. While the high level Verstappen operates at is so familiar it can almost be taken for granted (his superb second place in Hungary, for example), Hadjar has done a more than respectable job alongside him so far.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Hearn Targets Brandon Moore Next For Teremoana
Sports.content:
“I think we might fight him next, Brandon Moore,” Hearn said after the fight. “We have really got to find someone. It’s so frustrating in Australia because no one wants to fight him.”

A fight with Moore (19-1, 10 KOs) would provide an obvious measuring stick. He defeated Savage by a 10-round unanimous decision last September, dropping him in the seventh. His lone defeat came against Richard Torrez Jr., who knocked him out in five rounds in 2024.

Hearn felt Savage became frightened once he experienced Teremoana’s power.

“I was disappointed Savage didn’t get [further]. I don’t blame him, but it was just the fear. His eyes were popping out of his head as soon as he felt the power.”

Teremoana hardly pressed the accelerator in the opening round, throwing only a handful of punches before hurting Savage with a right hand late. Hearn liked the patience he showed rather than immediately going for the finish.

“I saw a guy that was a little bit more experienced tonight. Sort of took his time. I mean, he could have really done it in 30 seconds.”

Getting meaningful rounds has become increasingly difficult. Hearn conceded that fans will question the quality of Teremoana’s opposition and said Matchroom has reached the point where the competition must increase.

“There’ll be a lot of the public that will say, ‘Well, who’s he fighting?’ And I get that as well. We’ve got to step up,” Hearn said. “We do really, really need rounds.”

Hearn wants Teremoana to fight twice more this year and believes another four or five bouts are needed before he challenges for a world heavyweight title. His target is the back end of 2027, when Teremoana will be 29.

“He needs someone that can take him five or six rounds,” Hearn said. “Sooner or later there’s going to be a 10-round, 12-round war in there, and he’ll be ready.”

Anthony Joshua has also taken notice of Teremoana.

“AJ said to me a few times, ‘What’s this Teremoana?’ I’m like, ‘He’s a fucking monster.’”

Hearn expects a different type of fight once Teremoana encounters heavyweights willing and capable of attacking him rather than simply trying to survive.

Sports.title: Jake Paul’s MVP Signs IBF Champion Elif Turhan
Sports.content:
Turhan gives Jake Paul’s promotion another major piece at 135 pounds. Caroline Dubois holds the WBC and WBO championships, while Stephanie Han owns the WBA belt.

That leaves MVP working with fighters who control all four major lightweight titles.

Turhan punched her way into that company last December in Monte Carlo. She broke down Brazilian Olympic gold medalist Beatriz Ferreira and forced a fifth-round stoppage to seize the IBF crown, registering the defining victory of her professional career.

She has since strengthened her position with wins over Taylah Gentzen in January and Gabriella Tellez in June.

Turhan brings pressure and finishing instinct to a division loaded with potential championship fights. She likes to close the distance, force exchanges and punish opponents once her combinations begin finding the target.

The Istanbul fighter becomes the first Turkish boxer to join MVP and follows Nicolson as the second addition produced by the promotion’s agreement with Matchroom.

Turhan believes the partnership can push her toward more championship opportunities.

“I am incredibly excited to be part of this powerful collaboration. This marks a major signal of the exciting initiatives we will undertake for women’s boxing globally, and I am deeply honored to be involved in this journey with all my strength and energy.”

Her next opponent has yet to be confirmed, but her ambitions reach beyond defending the IBF belt.

“I am excited for the opportunities that will come my way as I look to win more major World Titles.”

That pursuit creates an obvious pressure point at lightweight. Dubois controls two belts, Han holds another and Turhan carries the IBF championship.

If MVP eventually matches its lightweight champions, Turhan will have to establish her pressure against fighters capable of controlling distance, countering her entries and punishing her on the way inside.

Sports.title: Teremoana vs. DeAndre Savage Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana improved to 12-0 with a second-round knockout of DeAndre Savage after another destructive heavyweight finish. Savage survived the opening round despite absorbing several heavy shots as Teremoana began finding his distance and opening up. That resistance ended quickly in the second. Teremoana cracked Savage with a big punch that buckled the American’s legs but left him standing. The Australian kept hunting the finish, dropped Savage moments later, and watched as he failed to beat the referee’s count. Savage became only the third opponent to take Teremoana beyond the opening round, but the extra three minutes merely delayed another knockout for the Australian heavyweight.

Michael Zerafa broke down Alejandro Ortiz for a stoppage victory on the Gold Coast after taking command in the later rounds. Zerafa began forcing Ortiz onto the back foot, then cracked him with a heavy shot in the seventh as the pressure increased. His corner demanded he keep letting his hands go while staying smart, telling him Ortiz was hurt whenever he opened up. Zerafa responded by pressing harder and keeping Ortiz under fire. The breakthrough came when Zerafa dropped Ortiz and immediately looked to close the show. Ortiz climbed off the canvas but remained hurt, and the fight was stopped soon afterward when he had taken enough. The victory gave Zerafa the result he needed after entering the fight under pressure and facing questions over his recent form.

Sports.title: Jack Dempsey’s Harry Wills Problem Never Went Away
Sports.content:
Following Jack Johnson’s 1910 victory over Jim Jeffries, racial violence erupted across the United States. The possibility of another Black heavyweight challenging a white champion encountered resistance from promoters, regulators, and others concerned about another interracial title fight.

Wills paid heavily for that environment.

A Dempsey-Wills fight nearly materialized in 1922 when promoter Tex Rickard selected a date and had tickets printed for a proposed bout in New Jersey. The promotion collapsed when the financing needed to meet Dempsey’s guarantee failed.

Another attempt ran into opposition in New York, where athletic commission chairman William Muldoon resisted an interracial heavyweight championship fight over concerns about racial unrest.

Dempsey also gave his critics ammunition. He drew the color line early in his championship reign before later changing his public position. His long stretches of inactivity intensified criticism that Wills was being denied an opportunity he had earned. Yet Wills himself resisted blaming Dempsey.

“My only regret in life is that I never got a shot at Dempsey, [and] I’m sure I could have beaten him,” Wills later said. “It wasn’t Jack’s fault. He wasn’t scared of anyone. He was a great fighter.”

Dempsey lost the heavyweight championship to Gene Tunney in 1926. Wills never fought for the world title.

The missing fight should count when Dempsey’s championship reign is evaluated. Wills was precisely the type of challenger a champion needed to defeat to remove questions about his dominance.

Placing the entire responsibility on Dempsey, however, ignores the racial barriers, regulators, promoters and failed financing that repeatedly interfered with the fight.

More than a century later, nobody knows what would have happened if Jack Dempsey and Harry Wills had finally met. That unanswered question is why Wills remains an unavoidable part of Dempsey’s legacy.

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Dismisses Shakur Stevenson’s Vacant-Belt Championships
Sports.content:
“This fight is about Teofimo Lopez trying to get the world title again, become a real three-division world champion. No vacant belts,” Lopez Sr. said to Fighthype. “Shakur got like two vacant belts, right? So, to me, he’s not a real three-division world champion. My son is going to do it the right way. We’re going to go straight to the champion. No vacant belt.”

Stevenson has actually won world titles across four divisions. His first came against Joet Gonzalez for the vacant WBO featherweight belt in 2019. He then stopped reigning WBO junior lightweight champion Jamel Herring in 2021 before defeating Edwin De Los Santos for the vacant WBC lightweight title in November 2023.

The fourth belt is difficult for Lopez Sr. to dismiss under his own standard. Shakur took the WBO light welterweight title from Teofimo in January, giving him two divisional championships won by defeating reigning titleholders.

Lopez Sr. also criticized Shakur’s fighting style and questioned how much further Stevenson can climb through the weight classes.

“I would love to fight him again. Let’s hope that we can get him before we move up too high,” Lopez Sr. said. “I don’t think Shakur can go up in the weight divisions. He’s too chinny. He doesn’t like to get hit. He’s a boring fighter.”

He believes Teofimo fought the wrong fight against Shakur. In his view, Teofimo should have boxed from the back foot instead of following the southpaw to his right all night.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Answers Devin Haney’s IBF Call
Sports.content:
“Have the WBO.. I want the IBF,” Devin said on X.

Haney seems to have signaled his preferred opponent without directly naming him. The choice makes sense. Paro brings a large following in Australia and the potential for a PPV event built around two welterweight champions.

That separates Paro from Jack Catterall, another opponent who has been discussed for Haney. Catterall presents a difficult fight with his movement, defense, timing and awkward southpaw style.

Paro is a southpaw as well, but he’s much more willing to engage and turn fights into physical exchanges. Haney has generally performed well against aggressive fighters who come forward, giving him opportunities to box from range, counter, and tie up when they get inside.

Catterall offers a different challenge. He’s unlikely to chase Haney recklessly or provide the type of pressure that allows Haney to settle into his preferred rhythm. Taking that fight would mean accepting considerable stylistic difficulty without getting another world title in return.

Paro gives Haney the opportunity to unify the division while bringing an established Australian audience to the promotion. From Haney’s perspective, that combination makes the matchup easier to understand commercially.

Nothing has been finalized, but the exchange leaves little mystery about their interest. Both champions have publicly opened the door to putting the IBF and WBO titles together.

Sports.title: Archie Moore Silences Yvon Durelle in Montreal Rematch
Sports.content:
The rematch drew 11,555 spectators, generating a gate of $140,519 to set a Montreal boxing record. Former world heavyweight champion Jack Sharkey served as referee.

Moore, already well into his 40s, had held the light heavyweight crown since defeating Joey Maxim in December 1952. Durelle, 29, remained a leading contender after his ferocious effort in their initial meeting.

Rather than trading immediately with the heavy-handed challenger, Moore fought cautiously through the opening two rounds. His defense limited Durelle’s opportunities to land the kind of power shots that had caused so much trouble in their first fight.

Two judges had Moore in front after two rounds, while the third had the fight even.

Moore changed the fight completely in the third. A hard right hand dropped Durelle, who beat the count at seven and tried to fight back. The champion quickly closed in.

Three more knockdowns followed as Moore connected with rights and lefts. After the fourth knockdown of the round, Sharkey counted Durelle out at 2:52.

Moore had turned a rivalry born from one of the greatest scares of his championship reign into a decisive three-round knockout.

Durelle faced difficult circumstances before the fight. A boating accident left him with a back injury, and his hometown of Baie-Sainte-Anne suffered the tragic Escuminac Disaster in June, when 35 fishermen lost their lives.

Moore continued his remarkable run near the top of the sport. Durelle later challenged George Chuvalo for the Canadian heavyweight title in November 1959, losing by knockout in the 12th round.

The two rivals eventually became friends. Moore retained enormous respect for Durelle, remembering him as one of the hardest punchers and toughest opponents he faced.

Their first fight became the classic. On August 12, 1959, Moore made the rematch his answer.

Ghana News.title: BoG Governor urges banks to redesign loans for agriculture-focused SMEs
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Asiama, BoG Governor

The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has urged banks to develop more innovative and flexible credit products tailored to the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly businesses operating along the agricultural value chain.

He said despite the improvement in Ghana’s economic conditions and a strong rebound in credit creation, many SMEs in the agricultural sector continue to struggle to access financing because banks perceive them as relatively high-risk businesses.

Dr Asiama made the call when he engaged Chief Executive Officers and heads of banks, where he outlined recent developments in the economy and the banking sector.

“However, despite the improved economic environment and the growing demand for credit, many SMEs, particularly those on the agricultural value chain, still struggle to access finance, just because banks continue to perceive these businesses as relatively high risk,” he said.

The Governor argued that banks must move beyond traditional lending approaches and develop a better understanding of the sectors and businesses they finance.

“As banks, you are not merely financial intermediaries, you are important business partners in the growth and transformation of the economy,” Dr Asiama stated.

He specifically urged banks to design loan products that reflect the seasonal nature of agricultural businesses, particularly in determining repayment schedules.

“This should include developing innovative and flexible credit products that recognise the seasonal nature of agricultural activities and align loan repayment schedules with the timing and pattern of borrowers' cash flows,” he said.

According to the Governor, such an approach would make it easier for SMEs to secure financing under conditions that reflect the realities of their operations.

“Such an approach would enable SMEs to access financing on terms that better reflect the realities of their businesses,” he added.

The call comes as financial conditions in Ghana continue to ease, with the Bank of Ghana reporting a significant rebound in credit creation.

Private sector credit grew by 41.2% in June 2026, compared with 8.6% recorded in the same period a year earlier, while real private sector credit growth stood at 34.1%.

Dr Asiama said the improvement in financial conditions provides an opportunity for banks to increase their support for productive sectors of the economy.

He noted that interest rates in the money market have continued to moderate across various market segments, with these developments beginning to translate into stronger credit flows to the private sector.

The Governor also pointed to broader improvements in the banking sector, including stronger capitalisation and asset quality.

The industry’s capital adequacy ratio increased to 20.4% in June 2026, from 10.6% a year earlier, while the non-performing loan ratio declined to 16.1% from 23.1% over the same period.

With agriculture employing a significant proportion of businesses and households and serving as a key source of raw materials for industry, Dr Asiama’s call places renewed emphasis on ensuring that improved financial conditions translate into greater access to productive credit.

Ghana News.title: Black Queens demand outstanding bonuses and better support from government
Ghana News.content:
Ghana's senior women's national team, the Black Queens, have demanded the payment of outstanding bonuses and per diems while accusing the government of neglect and inadequate professional support during their campaign at the ongoing Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco.

The Black Queens exited the competition at the quarterfinal stage after a 2-1 defeat to Malawi, a result that ended Ghana's hopes of securing an automatic qualification spot for next year's FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil.

In a statement issued ahead of their World Cup playoff against Côte d'Ivoire on Thursday, the players expressed frustration over what they described as a general lack of support and called for improved treatment and better professional conditions in future national team assignments.

The players expressed disappointment at the level of official support during their WAFCON campaign, noting that the Sports Minister and President were present only at their first official training session.

Despite their concerns, the Black Queens stressed that the statement was not intended to create conflict or disrespect anyone, but rather to demand “transparency, accountability, fairness and respect.”

They also praised their technical staff for standing by them throughout the campaign and urged the relevant authorities to engage with the players and work towards a swift resolution.

The players also called for their outstanding financial obligations to be settled, while urging the relevant authorities to provide the necessary support to enable the team to compete at the highest level.

Ghana will face Côte d'Ivoire on Thursday with a place in the World Cup playoffs at stake.

Ghana News.title: Some Ghanaians have a way of boxing you – Perez Musik
Ghana News.content:
Award-winning gospel musician Perez Musik has criticised the tendency to place Ghanaian artistes in fixed musical categories, saying musicians should be allowed to explore different sounds without being defined by a single genre.

Speaking on The Career Trail on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, he said he faced difficulties both when urban gospel was not widely accepted within Christian circles and later when he began experimenting with contemporary sounds.

“One of the challenges was that it's not really an accepted genre in the country. The Christian fraternity hasn't come to terms with that aspect of the song ministry. So it was quite difficult,” he said.

Perez Musik explained that urban gospel provided an avenue for young Christians to express their faith through music that connected with their generation.

He later encountered a different form of resistance when he began exploring contemporary music.

“One of the challenges I faced when I say, in quotes, ‘transition’, was that the people in the contemporary side were like, ‘Ah, who's this? Is he part of us? Is he one of us? Where's he coming from?’” he said.

He stressed that the change was not an attempt to abandon urban gospel but rather an effort to explore his creativity.

“It wasn't intentional. It was just me expressing myself, like testing my limits. I still do urban gospel. My latest song has more of an urban Afro vibe. But I felt like I had to push myself, push my limits,” he said.

Perez Musik argued that artistes should be free to experiment with different musical styles as long as the message they communicate remains clear.

“I love to explore different sounds and I don't see anything wrong with that. I have a problem with it when people categorise and segment. I think it's just music,” he said.

He said musicians should be able to move between ballads, R&B, soul, alternative music and other styles without being restricted by the genre with which audiences first identify them.

For Perez Musik, the problem is partly rooted in how Ghanaian audiences associate people with the first thing for which they become known.

“Ghanaians have a way of boxing you. That's why we call every toothpaste, we call every bath soap Key Soap,” he said.

He said some people in the contemporary music space still do not regard him as a contemporary artiste because of his association with urban gospel.

Despite the challenges, Perez Musik said he remains grateful for the progress he has made.

“But I think it's just the grace of God that has brought me this far. It's just the grace and the mercy of God. And I don't take that for granted at all,” he said.

Ghana News.title: ECG announces power outages in parts of Greater Accra and Volta Region
Ghana News.content:
The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced power outages affecting parts of the Greater Accra and Volta regions due to damaged electricity infrastructure and emergency maintenance works.

In the Accra West Region, ECG said an outage affecting Sowutuom and surrounding communities was caused by broken high-tension poles at Sowutuom.

The affected areas include Sowutuom Mambo, Glorious Jesus, Ablekuma Fanmilk, Ablekuma Abease, God First, Roman Park, Piteo Junction, Vicollis and Olebu Melcom, as well as adjoining communities.

According to ECG, its engineers are working to repair the damaged infrastructure and restore electricity supply to the affected areas.

The company did not provide a specific restoration time for the Sowutuom outage but said its technical teams were attending to the fault.

ECG has also announced two separate emergency maintenance exercises in the Volta Region for Thursday, August 13.

The first exercise is scheduled to take place between 9:00 am and 4:00 pm to enable engineers to work on a fault affecting electricity supply.

Communities expected to experience the temporary outage include Sokode Ando, Sokode Gbagble, parts of Sokode Gborgame and surrounding areas.

A second emergency maintenance exercise will take place on the same day from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

The affected areas are Payin, Dzodze, Ziope, Akporkope, Agortime, Kpetoe and surrounding communities.

ECG said the planned interruptions are necessary to allow its engineers to carry out work on faults affecting the electricity network.

The company apologised for the inconvenience caused by the Sowutuom outage and the scheduled maintenance exercises, and said the work was being undertaken to address faults and restore reliable electricity supply.

Ghana News.title: Incumbent Western North NPP Regional Chairman withdraws from seeking re-election
Ghana News.content:
The incumbent Western North Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Benjamin Armah, has withdrawn from the race to seek re-election ahead of the party’s regional executive elections.

Mr Armah said the decision followed deep reflection and extensive consultations with his family, friends, and key stakeholders, as well as his desire to serve the broader interests of the NPP in the Western North Region.

In a statement issued in Sefwi Wiawso, he said the decision was not taken lightly but was necessary to prioritise the unity, stability, and strategic strength of the party over personal ambition.

“This is a moment for unity, not division; consolidation, not fragmentation; and collective purpose, not personal ambition,” he stated.

Mr Armah expressed appreciation to party members across the region, particularly constituency executives, electoral area coordinators, polling station executives, delegates, grassroots activists, elders, and patrons who supported his candidature.

He said after consultations with key stakeholders, he had decided to offer his “full and unequivocal support” to McDaniels Nyame.

Mr Armah described Mr Nyame as a dedicated party member with proven loyalty to the NPP’s traditions and values, as well as organisational competence and political maturity.

“Having had the opportunity to work closely with Mr McDaniels Nyame over the years, I have witnessed first-hand his dedication to the NPP.

“I am persuaded that he possesses the temperament, experience, organisational capacity, and leadership qualities required to consolidate our gains, heal divisions where they exist, energise our grassroots, and provide the strategic direction necessary to reposition the Western North Region for the political tasks ahead,” he said.

He consequently called on his supporters, delegates, and party executives who backed his candidature to transfer their confidence, energy, and support to Mr Nyame.

Mr Armah stressed that his decision to withdraw from the contest did not mean he was stepping away from party activities.

“My withdrawal from this contest does not represent a withdrawal from service to our Party. On the contrary, I remain fully committed to the New Patriotic Party and shall continue to serve, in whatever capacity necessary, with dedication, humility, loyalty, and integrity,” he said.

He further called on NPP members in the region to remain united to strengthen the party’s chances of winning the 2028 general election.

The Western North NPP is expected to hold its regional executive elections in the coming weeks as the party begins its reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general election.

Ghana News.title: Government targets local production of Zonda vehicle components under 24-hour economy
Ghana News.content:
Government is pushing for the local production of selected components used in vehicles assembled by Zonda as part of efforts to deepen Ghana’s manufacturing capacity and create more jobs under the 24-hour economy.

Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang said identifying vehicle parts that could be manufactured locally would create opportunities for Ghanaian businesses and expand employment across the manufacturing value chain.

“I will be very happy going forward if we can even isolate one or two parts that we can produce locally,” she said.

The Vice President made the remarks after observing operations at the Zonda vehicle assembly facility, where workers operate in shifts around the clock.

She said the continuous operations demonstrate the potential of the government’s 24-hour economy to increase production and create more employment opportunities.

Professor Opoku-Agyemang stressed the need for closer collaboration between government and local manufacturers to identify areas where Ghanaian companies can participate in the vehicle assembly value chain.

She said producing selected components locally would help strengthen domestic businesses while building the technical skills of Ghanaian workers.

It could also create opportunities for businesses in related industries that supply parts and services to the automotive sector.

Government therefore intends to work with manufacturers and other stakeholders to identify components that can be produced locally and gradually increase Ghanaian participation in vehicle production.

The initiative forms part of broader efforts to strengthen local industry, reduce reliance on imported components and retain more value within the Ghanaian economy.

Government believes expanding local content in vehicle assembly could also support the wider objectives of the 24-hour economy, particularly through increased production, industrialisation and job creation.

Ghana News.title: Telecel, MoMAG train agents to improve professionalism, compliance and customer service
Ghana News.content:
Telecel Ghana has partnered with the Mobile Money Advocacy Group Ghana (MoMAG) to train mobile money agents as part of efforts to improve their capabilities, professionalism and compliance with regulations.

‎The initiative, held under the theme “Amplifying the Impact; Building a Safe, Trusted and Profitable Agent Network,” seeks to strengthen the agent network, which remains a critical part of the mobile money ecosystem.

‎Speaking at the engagement, Samuel Sarpong, Sales and Distribution Director at Telecel Ghana, said agents play an important role in the growth of the company's telecom and mobile money business.‎

‎According to him, the training is intended to equip agents with the knowledge and skills required to provide better services to customers.‎

‎“We are working with the MoMAG of Ghana as a mobile money agent network to collaborate on our various efforts to improve their capability as agents.”‎

‎He added that the agent network is an important part of the telecom and cash business ecosystem, making continuous capacity building necessary.‎

‎“One of the best ways is to equip them through this kind of capacity training so that they'll be better positioned to serve our customers better.”‎

‎The President of the Mobile Money Advocacy Group Ghana, Edward Ofori Agyemang, said the partnership with Telecel is part of a broader effort to collaborate with electronic money issuers to address challenges confronting mobile money agents.‎

‎He cited fraud and attacks by armed robbers as some of the major threats facing agents across the country.‎

‎“We all know in the country how fraud is going on, how armed robbers are killing our agents.”‎

‎Mr Ofori Agyemang stressed the need for agents to receive continuous training to enable them to operate professionally and protect their businesses.‎

‎He also highlighted customer relations as an important area requiring attention, particularly for agents who may lack the skills to communicate effectively with customers.‎

‎“Some of the agents who don't know how to talk to customers, how to relate to customers, and customers are the people who give us the money.”‎

‎According to him, the collaboration with Telecel is therefore aimed at ensuring that agents understand how to run their businesses professionally and in accordance with applicable regulations.‎

‎“We have partnered with Telecel Ghana to train our agents to make sure that the businesses they are doing, they would make sure that they do everything in compliance with regulations.”‎

‎Top-performing agent welcomes initiative

‎For some agents, the training has provided an opportunity to gain new knowledge and better understand Telecel's mobile money operations.‎

‎James Ablo, a top-performing Telecel agent, described the programme as beneficial and said the lessons would help him improve his business.‎

‎“Today's program is very helpful to me. I've learned a lot.”‎

‎Mr Ablo disclosed that he had previously encountered some challenges with Telecel but said the engagement had given him a new perspective and useful information.‎

‎“I'm someone who has issues with Telecel, but now that I've been here today, it's my first time.”‎

‎He said the knowledge gained from the programme would help boost his business, particularly in relation to Telecel's mobile money services.‎

‎“I've learned something that is going to boost my business, especially in terms of Telecel mobile money issue.”‎

‎Mr Ablo also expressed his intention to share what he had learnt with people within his community and educate them about the benefits of Telecel's services.

‎“As I'm going, I hope I'm going to teach people around my area what the benefits in Telecel and so far what Telecel is doing for the country.”‎

‎The collaboration comes as mobile money agents continue to serve as an important point of access to digital financial services for customers across Ghana.‎

‎The organisers believe that equipping agents with knowledge in customer service, fraud awareness, regulatory compliance and business management will help strengthen trust within the mobile money ecosystem.‎

‎The initiative also seeks to ensure that agents can operate more professionally while building sustainable and profitable businesses.

‎For Telecel and MoMAG, the focus is ultimately on developing an agent network that is safe, trusted, professional and better equipped to serve customers.

Ghana News.title: Speaker Bagbin recalls Parliament for five-day sitting from August 24
Ghana News.content:
Ghana's Parliament

Speaker of Parliament Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin has recalled Parliament from recess for a five-day sitting to consider urgent parliamentary business.

The recall will begin on Monday, August 24, and continue until Friday, August 28, at Parliament House in Accra.

The directive was issued by the Speaker on Wednesday, August 12, in accordance with Order 58(4) of the Standing Orders of the Parliament of Ghana.

In the directive, Speaker Bagbin exercised the power granted to him under the Standing Orders to recall Parliament notwithstanding the recess.

The notice states that Parliament will sit from 12 noon on Monday, August 24, with proceedings continuing through Friday, August 28.

The Speaker said the recall had been necessitated by the need for Parliament to consider urgent parliamentary business, although the notice did not specify the particular matters to be dealt with during the sitting.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Trump remarks on diminishing impact of pro-Israel groups in Congress
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump took a jab at the dwindling power of pro-Israel lobbying groups in Congress and across Washington’s political spectrum in a pre-taped exclusive recording with the hyper-partisan show America Speaks on the MAGA-friendly network “Real America’s Voice” (RAV).

When asked by host Wayne Allyn Root in the interview that aired on Tuesday about the “problem,” of the “communist colour revolution”, taking over “the biggest cities in America”, Trump replied that the biggest change he had observed over the last decade is “what’s happened to Israel and Jewish people”, adding that if, “you go back 20, 25 years ago, they had the most powerful lobby in Washington. Now, everyone is … if you look at the House … you look at the Democrats in the House … it’s pretty amazing actually. I’ve never seen anything like it.”

The comments come after a recent survey by The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs revealed a dramatic erosion of support for the US ally, with burgeoning opposition from Democrats and signs of polarisation among the Republican base.

This was not the first time the president had conceded Israel’s declining support in US politics. In September 2025, an interview with White House correspondent Reagan Reese of the Daily Caller, a right-wing website founded by former Fox News personality Tucker Carlson, saw Trump acknowledging that he was aware of slumping support for Israel among young Republicans, later explaining to the Caller that Israel’s ironclad endorsement in Congress is now a thing of the past.



In the 42-minute audio clip with RAV, Trump went on to slight Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, the highest-ranking Jewish official in US history and a reliably pro-Israel voice, “Look at Schumer. He’s become virtually a Palestinian,” he told the Caller.

Trump made similar comments in 2025, as well. During a March 2025 Oval Office meeting, Trump told reporters that “Schumer is a Palestinian, as far as I’m concerned,” and reiterated the comment at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in July. He berated the Democrat whom he claims was once “one hundred percent for Israel”.

At the time, Trump’s derogatory proclamations met with widespread disapproval and drew condemnation from Jewish and Muslim groups over what many saw as a xenophobic slur, regarding the president’s attempts to frame “Palestinian” as a political insult directed at Schumer.

In March 2024, the Senate minority leader had called for a leadership shake-up in Israel, after describing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as “too willing to tolerate the civilian toll in Gaza”.

That was the Jewish-American Democrat’s most vociferous critique of Israel since its genocidal war in Gaza first began in October 2023, having also expressed support for a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The veteran senator is usually a staunch defender of Israel.

More recently, Schumer reprimanded the president over his handling of the US-Israel war on Iran, noting that his “rinse and repeat approach … isn’t a strategy”, but a “recipe for utter disaster”, adding, “we keep moving backward … it’s incredible what a fiasco this war is.”
