World.title: CBN reverses OMO restriction, opens market to local investors
World.content:
CBN Governor, Yemi Cardoso

*Individuals, corporates, non-bank institutions now eligible

* Lifts tenored repo suspension

*Removes FX, govt securities restrictions on Discount Window access

By Babajide Komolafe

The Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, yesterday reversed its seven-year restriction on local investors’ participation in Open Market Operations, OMO, opening the market to individuals, corporates and non-bank financial institutions.

The restriction was introduced in 2019, in a bid to reduce pressure on the Naira, direct more lending to the real sector and drive down interest rates.

The reversal of the restriction was contained in a circular titled “Review of Discount Window Restrictions and Open Market Operations Participation Framework,” dated August 12, 2026 and signed by Okey Umeano, Ag. Director, Financial Markets Department.

Under the revised framework, the CBN said: “OMO participation (primary and secondary markets) shall be open to all eligible investors through Deposit Money Banks (DMBs).”

It specifically listed “individuals, corporates and non-bank financial institutions” among eligible investors, adding that DMBs “shall continue to submit bids and settle transactions on behalf of their customers.”

The apex bank also removed restrictions on access to its Discount Window arising from participation in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, and primary auctions of government securities.

According to the circular, “Restrictions on access to the Discount Window arising from participation in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) are hereby removed.

“Restrictions on access to the Discount Window arising from participation in the primary auctions of Government securities are hereby removed.

“The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has reviewed existing market practices and developments in the foreign exchange, money, and fixed-income markets. The Bank has also reviewed the framework governing access to the Standing Lending Facility (SLF), Tenored Repo Operations and participation in Open Market Operations (OMO).”

The apex bank also lifted the suspension of Tenored Repo Operations, allowing it to conduct repo transactions across approved tenors of between four and 90 days.

It said: “The suspension of Tenored Repo Operations is hereby lifted,” the CBN stated, adding that the operations would support “effective liquidity management, improve money market functioning and enhance monetary policy implementation.”

The reopening of the OMO market to domestic investors is expected to provide individuals, companies and non-bank financial institutions with another avenue for investing in short-term securities, while potentially deepening activity in the money market.

The CBN, however, retained control over the scale and timing of OMO issuance, stating that “the volume, tenor and frequency of OMO issuances shall continue to be determined by the CBN in line with prevailing liquidity conditions and monetary policy objectives.”

It also retained the existing single-bid auction structure for OMO transactions.

The new framework takes immediate effect, with the CBN directing all banks, authorised dealers and market participants to ensure strict compliance.

World.title: Osun election: ADC not withdrawing for any party – Spokesperson
World.content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

The African Democratic Congress, ADC, in Osun State has reiterated that it is not withdrawing from the Saturday governorship election nor working with any other party.

A statement issued by the ADC’s spokesperson in the State, Abosede Oluwaseun, on Wednesday, urged the electorate to disregard misinformation in the public that its candidate, Dr Najeem Salaam, has withdrawn from the election.

The ADC disclosed that the party is certain of victory and will not jeopardize its chances for any other political party; hence, it urged the people to go out on Saturday to vote for the party’s candidate.

The attention of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Osun State Chapter, has been drawn to the deliberate falsehood being circulated in some quarters that our party has stepped down for another political party. This is a blatant lie and a desperate political fabrication.

ADC has not stepped down for anybody, and we will not step down for anybody. Our position remains clear and unequivocal: those who desire electoral victory under the ADC banner should come and join us. ADC is not joining anybody.

The party said its national leaders and the Presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, have spoken with the people on the need to elect the party’s candidate as the governor of the state; hence, it has no reason to step down for any party.

The facts are already before the people of Osun. Our National Chairman was in Osun at the Freedom Park to campaign for our party. Our Presidential Candidate, Atiku Abubakar, was also here to canvass support for ADC. Our National Secretary, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola, the architect of modern Osun, has stood firmly with our Governorship Candidate, Dr. Najeem Salaam.

The candidate, Dr. Salaam himself, has continued his statewide engagement across towns and communities. These are not the actions of a party preparing to step down; they are the actions of a party fully committed to victory.

“We therefore call on those behind these shenanigans, falsehoods and politically motivated rumours to stop misleading the people. ADC is in this election to win, and Dr. Najeem Salaam Iwaloye remains the candidate to beat.

“Anyone who believes in the ADC platform and wants to join us is welcome. But let it be stated once again, for the avoidance of doubt: ADC has not stepped down, ADC is not stepping down, and ADC will step down for nobody”, the party added.

World.title: Air Peace loses N2bn to union picketing, seeks FG investigation
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Following the picketing of Nigeria’s largest airline, Air Peace, by aviation unions, Wednesday, the airline has disclosed that it lost more than N2 billion in revenue as a result of the industrial action.

The disruption followed a three days ultimatum issued on August 7 by the National Union of Air Transport Employees, NUATE, and the Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, ATSSSAN, to the Airline Operators of Nigeria, AON, demanding the remittance of the five per cent Ticket Sales Charge, TSC, and an end to what they described as the continued refusal by some airlines to allow the unfettered unionisation of their workers.

When the issues remained unresolved, the unions, backed by the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress, TUC, proceeded with the industrial action, picketing Air Peace’s operations at the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, and the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja.

Meanwhile, the airline’s Chief Operating Officer, Oluwatoyin Olajide, Wednesday, also said should affected passengers seek compensation, the unions responsible for the picketing would be held liable for the consequences of their actions.

Addressing newsmen at Air Peace’s headquarters in Lagos, she urged Federal Government, security agencies, airport authorities and aviation regulators to conduct a thorough and independent investigation into the incident.

Her words: “The disruption has caused significant financial damage to Air Peace, estimated at over N2 billion, while thousands of passengers had their journeys disrupted. Our passengers equally have constitutional rights, including the right to travel without unlawful interference.

“Yesterday, some of our employees were physically assaulted while peacefully expressing that choice, including a female employee who was left bleeding and bruised. We ask: how can workers’ rights be defended by violently attacking workers exercising their own constitutional rights?

“The incident also raises serious questions about airport security. How were individuals able to gain access to and disrupt operations within a highly controlled airport environment? Airports are sensitive national assets, and such violence should never be allowed to occur with impunity. The incident has also caused concern among our international partners and aircraft lessors and raises legitimate questions about confidence in Nigeria’s aviation business environment.

“What happened yesterday was a flagrant disrespect and disregard of extant laws and the subsisting judgement of the Federal High Court of Nigeria obtained on April 26, 2024, by the Staff and Employees of Air Peace against the NLC, TUC, NUATE, the Inspector General of Police and all other unions.

“The judgement declared that it is unlawful and unconstitutional for all these unions to threaten the employees of Air Peace through coercion of their employer, Air Peace, whether directly or indirectly, including through their officers, servants/agents, privies or other third parties, or howsoever to seek to impose membership of the unions upon the employees against their will.

“The court also granted an order of perpetual injunction restraining the unions from harassing the employees of Air Peace by any means at their places of work or any other place and to refrain from causing or instigating any breach of the peace likely to occasion harm to the staff and employers or any threat to their lives and property of Air Peace.

“The court also ordered the police to ensure compliance with this judgement throughout the federation. This appalling disruptive activity by the union members simply violated International Civil Aviation Regulation, ICAO, & NCAR Security regulation which, in simple terms, is an act of unlawful interference and is punishable under extant aviation regulations.

“The union members involved may be subject to no fly or arrest abroad if the matter is taken up appropriately. They should therefore be advised to watch and never cross the red line again.”

World.title: Osun Election: Adeleke Campaign Council petitions IGP over Senator Fadahunsi’s comments
World.content:
The Imole Campaign Council has petitioned the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, over recent comments attributed to Senator Francis Fadahunsi ahead of the August 15 Osun State governorship election.

In the petition dated August 12, 2026, the council drew the police’s attention to what it described as an “extremely disturbing video recording” allegedly showing the Osun East senator making comments calling for violence against members and supporters of the Accord Party.

The petition quoted Fadahunsi as allegedly saying, “From now on, whenever you see Accord members, kill them. I authorise you to kill them.” It also alleged that he said voters would not be allowed to cast their ballots even if they presented their voter cards.

The council described the alleged remarks as “extremely grave,” arguing that they could constitute a threat to lives, public peace and the security of the state.

It urged the police to investigate and authenticate the video, invite Fadahunsi for questioning and determine whether any individuals or groups had acted on the alleged comments.

The campaign council also called for adequate security at polling units and collation centres, stressing that “No Nigerian should have to fear being attacked or killed because of the political party he or she supports.”

It further urged the police to take preventive measures before the alleged threat could materialise, particularly with the governorship election approaching.

The petition also requested that security be provided for members and supporters of political parties across affected areas, while urging the police to ensure that voters can participate in the election without intimidation, harassment or violence.

The council said the petition was not intended to prejudge Fadahunsi, but to ensure that the allegations were properly investigated. It stated that “Political office must never become immunity from investigation.”

The petition was signed by Pelumi Olanjegbesi, Esq., on behalf of the campaign council.

World.title: Abiola’s death in custody should be reinvestigated — Falana
World.content:
Falana

LAGOS — Human rights lawyer, Mr Femi Falana, SAN, has called on the Federal Government to reopen investigations into the circumstances surrounding the death of the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale (M.K.O.) Abiola while in government custody in 1998.

Falana, who represented the Abiola family before the Oputa Panel on Human Rights Abuse, said a fresh investigation was necessary to establish the circumstances surrounding Abiola’s death and address unresolved questions raised by evidence presented before the panel.

Abiola who was widely recognised as the winner of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, declared himself president on June 12, 1994. He was subsequently arrested by the military government of General Sani Abacha and detained after being charged with treasonable felony.

Disclosing this in a statement he personally sent to Vanguard, Falana opined Abiola remained in custody for about four years and was subjected to prolonged detention despite concerns about his health.

He recalled that Archbishop Desmond Tutu, who visited Nigeria in April 1998, had expressed concern about Abiola’s deteriorating health and called for his release to enable him to receive appropriate medical attention.

According to Falana, the death of General Abacha on June 8, 1998, led to the emergence of General Abdulsalami Abubakar as Head of State, but Abiola was not released despite the release of several political prisoners.

Abiola died on July 7, 1998, shortly after meeting a visiting American delegation.

Falana said the circumstances surrounding the death were subsequently examined by the Oputa Panel, established by the Olusegun Obasanjo administration to investigate human rights abuses committed during the years of military rule.

He noted that Abubakar declined to appear before the panel to explain his role in the events surrounding Abiola’s detention and death.

Falana also referred to Abubakar’s recently published autobiography, Call of Duty, in which the former military leader rejected allegations that Abiola was poisoned, relying on an autopsy by foreign pathologists which reportedly attributed the death to natural causes.

However, Falana argued that the medical evidence did not resolve questions surrounding Abiola’s treatment while in detention.

He cited the account of Susan Rice, who was part of the American delegation that met Abiola shortly before his death, saying she had observed signs of ill health during the meeting.

Falana also referred to evidence before the Oputa Panel concerning the circumstances under which tea was served to Abiola during the meeting with the American delegation.

He said ACP Zadok, who had been responsible for Abiola’s security between 1996 and 1998, testified that he routinely tasted food, water or tea prepared for Abiola before it was served to him.

According to Falana, Zadok told the panel that he was removed from his duty post on the day of the American delegation’s visit.

He further said Major A.S. Aliyu, who was then Chief Security Officer to the Head of State, confirmed before the panel that Rice served tea to Abiola without tasting it.

Falana said the evidence presented before the panel raised questions about the security arrangements surrounding the visit and the circumstances of Abiola’s death.

He also cited the memoir of former United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan, who reportedly acknowledged that Abiola had been denied adequate medical care throughout his incarceration.

According to Falana, Annan also disclosed that he had urged Abubakar to release Abiola, but that the military government wanted him to abandon his claim to the presidency as a condition for his release.

Falana said the Oputa Panel, after reviewing the evidence before it, concluded that the government of the time knew more about the circumstances surrounding Abiola’s death than it had admitted.

The panel, he noted, also concluded that Abiola’s death was linked to his incarceration and denial of adequate medical attention, while describing the circumstances of his death as suspicious.

Falana quoted the panel as recommending a thorough investigation to establish what caused Abiola’s death.

He said the recommendation remained relevant, particularly in view of the continuing disagreements over the circumstances surrounding the death.

“Chief Moshood Abiola’s death was the result of his incarceration and the denial of access to adequate medical attention,” Falana quoted the panel as stating.

The lawyer said the Federal Government should act on the panel’s recommendation and reopen the investigation.

He argued that such an investigation would help clarify unresolved questions surrounding Abiola’s death and provide Nigerians with a definitive account of what happened to him while in government custody.

“Thus, the Oputa Panel came to the conclusion that Chief Moshood Abiola’s death was the result of his incarceration and the denial of access to adequate medical attention,” Falana said.

“In view of the denial of Abubakar and the members of the American delegation of any involvement in the suspicious death of Abiola, the Federal Government should, without any further delay, reopen investigation into the case.”

Falana said a fresh investigation would, as recommended by the Oputa Panel, “throw light to and inform the Nigerian people on what killed Chief Moshood Abiola” while in the custody of the Abubakar military government.

World.title: Photos: US, Nigeria hold fresh security talks in Washington
World.content:
The United States-Nigeria joint working group is holding a fresh round of talks in Washington DC, with security cooperation and counterterrorism measures featuring prominently on the agenda.

National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, led the Nigerian delegation at Wednesday’s meeting, while Allison Hooker, US Under-Secretary of State, headed the American team.

Among the Nigerian officials attending the meeting are the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu; Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa; and Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo.

According to the agenda for the meeting, discussions include counterterrorism efforts, progress made in bilateral cooperation and the next steps required to strengthen collaboration between both countries.

A bilateral defence meeting between Nigeria and the US is also scheduled to take place on Thursday.

The joint working group was established following the decision by US President Donald Trump to redesignate Nigeria as a “country of particular concern” (CPC).

The two countries previously held the inaugural meeting of the group in Abuja in January as part of efforts to deepen cooperation on security and other areas of mutual interest.

Both governments have reiterated their commitment to protecting religious freedom and advancing fundamental rights in Nigeria, including freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and freedom of religion or belief.

World.title: Osun Election: Political ambition not worth blood of Nigerians — Accord
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — The Accord Party has called for the immediate prosecution of Senator Francis Adenigba Fadahunsi over what it described as an alleged call for the killing of its members and supporters in Ijeshaland, Osun State, ahead of Saturday’s governorship election.

The party said the alleged remarks, contained in a campaign video circulating widely on social media, had raised fresh fears over the safety of voters and political supporters as the state heads to the polls, insisting that no political contest should put citizens’ lives at risk.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Joseph Omorogbe, Accord said Fadahunsi, who represents Osun East Senatorial District, allegedly made the remarks while addressing members of the All Progressives Congress during a campaign in Ijeshaland.

The party urged security agencies to act swiftly to prevent the alleged threat from escalating into violence.

“His outburst is outrageous and reprehensible, and has heightened the political tension in the state ahead of the governorship election,” Accord said.

The party called on the Inspector-General of Police and Director-General of the Department of State Services to apprehend Fadahunsi and take steps to rein in his supporters and alleged APC thugs.

Accord argued that the alleged remarks were particularly troubling coming from a serving senator only days before the election, saying political competition should never become a licence to threaten the lives of opponents.

“For a sitting senator to condescend so low to publicly threaten the lives of fellow compatriots days to the gubernatorial poll in the state is unjust and unacceptable,” the party said.

The party also alleged that more than 60 of its members had been arrested and detained in Abuja and Nasarawa State in a move it claimed was aimed at keeping them away from Saturday’s election.

It further alleged that the Police were planning to arrest more of its leaders and members before the poll, describing the alleged arrests as part of a wider effort to restrict its presence and create an advantage for the APC.

“This theatre of the absurd and fear mongering must stop forthwith,” Accord said.

The party alleged that its members and supporters across Osun had been subjected to political violence, harassment, intimidation and arrests by thugs it claimed were associated with the APC, with the alleged activities carried out in collusion with the Police and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission.

Accord demanded the immediate release of those it described as illegally detained and urged the relevant authorities to ensure that all political parties and their supporters could participate freely in the election.

It also appealed to the international community, including the European Union Delegation to Nigeria, United States Embassy, United Kingdom Embassy, African Union and ECOWAS, to closely monitor developments in Osun and condemn what it described as activities capable of undermining democracy.

“The people demand a free, fair, credible, inclusive and peaceful governorship election that meets international standards,” the party said.

Accord urged Osun voters to come out and exercise their franchise without fear, stressing that the choice of governor should be determined by the electorate rather than intimidation or violence.

“Accord prepares for an election, not war. The political ambition of anybody is not worth the blood of fellow citizens,” the party said.

The party called on all stakeholders to resist any attempt to manipulate the electoral process in favour of any political party and allow voters to freely choose their governor.

“Let the Osun electorate freely choose their governor. Any attempt to undermine the electoral process in favour of a political party must be resisted by all stakeholders,” Accord said.

It then urged its supporters to vote for Governor Ademola Adeleke, describing him as the leader they trusted to continue his work in the state.

The party described Saturday’s election as a defining moment for Osun and urged voters to support Accord, which it said was first on the ballot, insisting that its victory would herald peace and prosperity in the state.

World.title: Osun Election: Hashim warns against violence, calls for peaceful election
World.content:
Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim

OSOGBO — The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr Gbenga Hashim, has warned political actors and supporters against inciting violence ahead of the Osun State governorship election scheduled for Saturday.

Hashim, in a statement, said those making inflammatory statements or encouraging violence could face legal consequences, urging all stakeholders to allow voters to exercise their franchise peacefully.

His warning followed reports of a comment allegedly made by Senator Francis Fadahunsi, representing Osun East Senatorial District, concerning members of the Accord Party ahead of the election.

Although Fadahunsi has reportedly denied making the statement attributed to him, the comment generated reactions across the country.

Hashim described alleged calls for violence during elections as unacceptable, stressing that political differences should not be allowed to threaten lives or undermine the electoral process.

He said relevant security and law enforcement agencies should investigate any allegation of incitement and take appropriate action where wrongdoing is established.

Hashim also urged political leaders, candidates and their supporters to exercise restraint and avoid statements capable of escalating tension in the state.

“We want to let everyone know that these actions would not go unpunished,” he said.

He further alleged that some Accord supporters had been victims of violence, adding that the party would continue to pursue lawful avenues to protect its members and supporters.

Meanwhile, the Osun State Police Command has invited Fadahunsi for questioning over the alleged comment.

The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, according to Hashim’s statement, said the senator had been invited and that the command would take further steps if he failed to honour the invitation.

The development comes as political parties intensify campaigns and mobilisation ahead of Saturday’s governorship election, with security agencies expected to maintain law and order and ensure the safety of voters and electoral officials.

World.title: Youths Must Become Custodians of Nigeria’s Democracy, Says FCC Chairman
World.content:
The Executive Chairman of the Federal Character Commission (FCC), Mrs. Ayo Hulayat Omidiran, has charged Nigerian youths to move beyond being mere beneficiaries of democracy and assume their rightful place as active stakeholders, custodians and builders of the nation’s democratic future.

Omidiran gave the charge in a goodwill message delivered on her behalf by the Federal Commissioner representing Enugu State in the FCC, Hon. Peter Ogbonna Eze, at a programme organised by the Nigeria Youth Organization with the theme, ‘The Role of Nigerian Youth in Consolidating the Gains of Democracy in Nigeria.’

The FCC chairman described the theme as timely and fundamental to the future of Nigeria, stressing that the sustainability and progress of the country’s democracy would depend substantially on the commitment, character, participation and leadership of the younger generation.

According to her, Nigerian youths possess the energy, creativity, innovation and intellectual capacity required to drive national development, adding that they must recognise that democracy extends beyond periodic elections.

She said democratic consolidation also requires respect for the rule of law, accountability, tolerance, peaceful participation, responsible citizenship, protection of fundamental rights and respect for Nigeria’s diversity.

Omidiran consequently urged young Nigerians to reject violence, hate speech, misinformation and other actions capable of weakening democratic institutions and national cohesion.

She also acknowledged the decision of the Nigeria Youth Organization to endorse President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a second term, describing the endorsement as an indication of the organisation’s confidence in the importance of continuity, stability and sustained implementation of government policies and programmes.

She noted that continuity in governance provides an opportunity for administrations to consolidate reforms, strengthen institutions and build on initiatives already commenced for the benefit of Nigerians.

The FCC boss further emphasised the importance of equity, inclusion and fairness in sustaining Nigeria’s democracy, noting that these principles remain central to the constitutional mandate of the commission.

She said young Nigerians, irrespective of their state of origin, ethnicity or background, deserved fair access to opportunities, adding that equitable inclusion would strengthen their confidence and commitment to nation-building.

Omidiran called on youths to occupy the frontlines of constructive engagement with government and democratic institutions, urging them not only to demand accountability but also to contribute ideas, proffer solutions and accept responsibility for the development of the country.

She commended the Nigeria Youth Organization for creating platforms capable of equipping young Nigerians with civic knowledge, leadership skills and opportunities for meaningful participation in governance.

The FCC chairman stressed that securing Nigeria’s future could not be achieved by government alone, but required a sustained partnership among government, civil society, communities and the nation’s youth.

She urged young Nigerians to participate actively in democratic processes, engage government constructively, innovate and provide responsible leadership, saying their energy should become a force for peace, their creativity a tool for development and their leadership a pathway to a more united and prosperous Nigeria.

“Let us build a Nigeria where every young person believes that his or her voice matters, where merit is rewarded, where opportunities are accessible, and where diversity is a source of strength rather than division,” she said.

Omidiran, who spoke on behalf of the FCC and the 5th Commission, commended the Nigeria Youth Organization for convening the programme and its continued commitment to youth development and democratic advancement.

She wished participants fruitful deliberations and a successful programme.

World.title: Yayi at 57: A Journey of Grace, Service and Political Destiny
World.content:
Femi Ogbonnikan

Monday, August 10 marks the 57th birthday of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known across political circles and grassroots communities as Yayi, representing Ogun West Senatorial District in the National Assembly. It is a day of immense gratitude, joy, and victory, for attaining this milestone, not by human power or political manoeuvrings, but by grace—the divine grace to navigate the complex trials, fierce storms, and shifting tides of time while many along the way have faltered or fallen. In a country ranked among those with low average life expectancy globally, reaching the age of 57 in good health, administrative vigour, and political relevance is no mean feat. By all standards, 57 is far more than a numerical figure; it is a celebration of personal resilience, unwavering devotion to public duty, and an unyielding commitment to human service.

This year’s milestone carries extraordinary political significance as it coincides with a defining moment in Ogun State’s modern history. It arrives at a juncture where the three-term federal lawmaker and current Chairman of the Senate Committee on Appropriations is widely recognized by his supporters as a central figure positioned for higher executive leadership as Governor of Ogun State under the banner of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in 2027.

Adeola’s political trajectory represents one of the most structured legislative careers in contemporary Nigerian democracy.

His journey in elective office began in Lagos State, where he served two terms in the Lagos State House of Assembly representing Alimosho Constituency II, playing a key role in drafting tax and revenue legislation that contributed to the state’s financial independence.

He subsequently transitioned to the federal legislature, serving a term in the House of Representatives as Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee, followed by two distinguished terms representing Lagos West in the Senate.

Demonstrating a deep connection to his ancestral roots, he relocated his political base to Ogun State and secured a decisive victory for the Ogun West Senatorial seat in 2023.

In Abuja, as Chairman of the Senate Committee on Appropriations, he occupies a strategic position at the heart of Nigeria’s national fiscal architecture, earning recognition for his detail-oriented approach and ability to translate legislative influence into projects and programmes of direct relevance to ordinary citizens.

In his home constituency, the impact of his stewardship is felt through the broad reach of the Yayi Empowerment Foundation, which has become a recognizable name across Ogun West and beyond.

From scholarship grants for indigent tertiary students to medical outreaches, infrastructure support, and financial grants for market women, farmers, and artisans, his developmental footprint extends across communities in the district.

Frequent town hall meetings, youth skills-acquisition schemes, and sustained support for traditional institutions have strengthened his grassroots connection. Yet, his political vision has increasingly transcended the boundaries of a single senatorial district.

Over recent years, Senator Adeola has expanded his political and developmental footprint across Ogun Central and Ogun East through infrastructure facilitation, rural electrification, educational interventions, road rehabilitation, empowerment programmes, and party reconciliation efforts, presenting himself to supporters as a statewide political figure.

As the political calendar turns toward 2027, the growing support for Senator Adeola’s governorship ambition stems from a combination of state-wide goodwill, financial expertise as a chartered accountant, legislative experience, and extensive federal connections.

Unlike politicians whose influence remains strictly localized, Adeola has sought to build bridges across Egba, Ijebu, Remo, and Yewaland. His empowerment initiatives and political engagements have reached communities beyond Ogun West, earning him recognition among community leaders, market associations, youth groups, and political stakeholders. Supporters argue that a state with Ogun’s industrial potential requires an executive who understands both the machinery of government and the complex process of attracting investment, infrastructure, and federal support.

This is particularly important because Ogun State occupies a strategic position in Nigeria’s economic landscape. Its proximity to Lagos, expanding industrial corridors, agricultural potential, educational institutions, and growing urban centres makes it a state with enormous possibilities. But possibilities alone do not produce development. They require competent planning, financial discipline, political stability, and the ability to connect local priorities with national opportunities.

It is in this regard that Adeola’s supporters consider his legislative experience and position in Abuja an important advantage. They believe that his familiarity with national institutions and budgetary processes could help Ogun State pursue major infrastructure and economic projects with greater speed and strategic focus.

It is precisely this political momentum that has made Senator Adeola a formidable force in Ogun politics—and, conversely, a difficult proposition for his political adversaries. Recognizing the scale of his statewide network, organizational strength, legislative profile, and financial independence, opponents within and outside the ruling party may see his emergence as a serious political challenge.

Consequently, the political contest has increasingly featured competing narratives, media criticism, petitions, arguments over zoning, and attempts to question his suitability for the governorship.

However, supporters of Senator Adeola maintain that these efforts have not substantially weakened his political standing. Negative narratives intended to question his loyalty, alienate his supporters, or portray his federal background as a disadvantage have, in their view, struggled against what they describe as visible realities on the ground.

When critics seek to diminish his contributions, his supporters point to roads, educational interventions, empowerment initiatives, scholarships, medical outreaches, and other projects associated with his public service.

In electoral politics, they argue, narratives ultimately have to compete with the lived experiences of citizens. The argument that zoning arrangements should automatically be used to bar his candidacy has similarly generated a wider debate within the state. Zoning has historically played an important role in managing political expectations and balancing representation among different parts of Ogun State.

Nevertheless, the question confronting political parties in every election cycle is how to balance fairness, inclusiveness, electability, competence, and the legitimate aspirations of different political blocs. Adeola’s supporters argue that the 2027 contest should ultimately be determined by the candidate who can unite the state, win the election, and provide effective governance.

For them, Ogun State requires a leader capable of looking beyond sectional interests. The state is made up of diverse political, cultural, economic, and geographical interests, and the next governor will need to build bridges among them.

Adeola’s political journey—from Lagos to the federal legislature and subsequently back to Ogun—gives his supporters a narrative of experience across different levels of government. They argue that this exposure has prepared him to understand the complexity of governance beyond the confines of a single constituency.

Furthermore, the notion that strong federal connections constitute a drawback for state governance reflects, in the view of his supporters, a misunderstanding of modern economic administration. In an era when states compete aggressively for federal infrastructure, investment opportunities, favourable policy interventions, and strategic economic partnerships, political access can become an important instrument of development.

Ogun State cannot afford to operate in isolation from the federal government. Supporters believe it needs a governor who understands Abuja, knows how federal institutions work, and can translate those relationships into tangible benefits for the people.

For these reasons, Senator Adeola remains, in the eyes of his supporters, one of the most formidable contenders for 2027.

His political structure is not an artificial creation assembled overnight for an election year, but a network developed through years of legislative activity, constituency engagement, political organization, and grassroots interaction.

His supporters include market women, young entrepreneurs, traditional leaders, artisans, farmers, professionals, students, and political actors who believe that his experience can provide the state with a new direction.

Yet beyond the political calculations surrounding 2027, a birthday is fundamentally a moment for reflection.

At 57, Senator Adeola has accumulated decades of experiences that have shaped his understanding of politics, governance, leadership, and human relationships. Public life is rarely a straight road. It is characterized by victories and disappointments, friendships and disagreements, praise and criticism.

The ability to remain relevant through those changing circumstances requires resilience, adaptability, discipline, and a clear sense of purpose. His journey demonstrates an enduring capacity to navigate those realities.

His 57th birthday, therefore, should not be viewed solely through the prism of the 2027 governorship contest.

It is also an opportunity to acknowledge a public servant who has spent a significant portion of his adult life in the service of his constituents and the wider public.

Whatever political disagreements may exist around him, his career has contributed to the evolving story of legislative representation in Nigeria.

The ultimate judgment of any political career, however, belongs not to supporters or opponents alone, but to history and, most importantly, to the people whose lives public leadership is supposed to improve.

As Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola celebrates his 57th birthday, he stands at a historic convergence of maturity, legislative experience, and executive aspiration.

What his supporters regard as his greatest political strength is not merely the size of his network, but the belief that he has acquired sufficient experience to confront the complex economic and administrative challenges facing Ogun State.

The conversations taking place across political caucuses, city centres, communities, and rural areas demonstrate that his political future will remain one of the defining issues in the state’s journey toward 2027.

In the final analysis, fifty-seven (57) years of life and service have prepared Senator Adeola for what may become the most consequential chapter of his political journey.

His story is one of persistence, reinvention, legislative engagement, grassroots connection, and an enduring determination to remain relevant in public service. As friends, associates, constituents, political allies, and well-wishers celebrate him today, the deeper message is one of gratitude for the journey already travelled and hope for the opportunities that lie ahead. Whether viewed through the lens of his legislative accomplishments, his constituency interventions, or his growing statewide political profile, his 57th birthday provides an appropriate moment to celebrate a life that has become deeply intertwined with the political evolution of Ogun State.

Ultimately, the road to 2027 will be determined by the choices of the people, the decisions of political parties, and the unfolding realities of the political season. But whatever the outcome, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola’s 57th birthday marks an important milestone in a remarkable public journey. It is a celebration of survival, service, ambition, and resilience; a reminder that political leadership is not merely about occupying office but about building relationships, creating opportunities, and leaving footprints that citizens can remember.

For Yayi and his supporters, the future remains full of possibilities. And as Ogun State looks toward another defining political chapter, the birthday celebration becomes more than a personal anniversary—it becomes a moment to reflect on the journey so far and the larger destiny that may yet unfold.

*Ogbonnikan writes from Okeagbede, in Imeko-Afon LGA of Ogun state.

World.title: FG Committed to Healthcare Delivery Nationwide, Says Permanent Secretary
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin

The Federal Government is committed to reshaping health delivery system in the country through innovative and funding of healthcare facilities across the nation.

The Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Daju Kachollom, disclosed this in Benin Wednesday during the inauguration of some projects at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) to mark one year anniversary of Prof. Idia Ize-Iyamu as the Chief Medical Director (CMD).

The permanent secretary, represented by the Medical Director of the National Orthopedic Hospital, Benin, Dr. Philip Ugbodaga, urged support for the President Bola Tinubu presidency to continue to energize the health sector for the good of all.

She affirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening healthcare delivery under President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

She praised the CMD, the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH), Benin, for actualizing the mandate that the ministry and the president has given her to help to transform and bring to the teeming masses the goodies of democracy.

Kachollom, who performed the unveiling of the Special Investigation Unit (SIU), among other projects, commended the CMD of the UBTH for her remarkable achievements in her first year in office.

She praised the CMD for her prudent management, visionary leadership, and efforts to improve infrastructure and clinical services, describing her as a beacon of hope and a trailblazer as the hospital’s first female chief medic.

Kachollom said the achievements recorded within 365 days demonstrated her commitment to transforming the hospital and improving healthcare delivery.

She pledged to submit a comprehensive report, supported by photographic evidence, to the Minister of Health for further commendation.

Facilities inspected include renovated security facilities, a 65-bed Accident and Emergency complex, an expanded mortuary upgraded from 72 to 460 chambers, a multi-faith centre, premium and regular renal dialysis units, a child-friendly paediatric clinic, a revitalised oxygen plant, a geriatric ward, a 160-slice CT scan, a special investigation unit, dental and oncology centres and improved theatre facilities.

Prof. Ize-Iyamu, the CMD, said that the extensive infrastructural and service upgrades undertaken by her administration is to improve patient care and experiences.

The CMD said the projects were driven by the need to provide patients with safe, dignified and world-class healthcare services.

The CMD stressed that UBTH remains a one-stop tertiary healthcare institution with specialist services covering neurosurgery, oncology, dentistry, eye care, renal services and other complex medical needs.

She reaffirmed the hospital’s commitment to providing quality healthcare to all patients irrespective of age, gender, tribe, religion or social status, noting that sickness knows no boundaries.

Ize-Iyamu also announced plans to extend its impact to underserved communities through its comprehensive health centre at Udo, where 5,000 people will receive free medical services, including cataract surgery and other treatments.

A new dental centre equipped with two dental chairs, mobile units and X-ray facilities will also be inaugurated at the centre.

She thanked the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, development partners, donors, staff and other stakeholders for their support, assuring them that UBTH would continue to improve its facilities and patient experience while remaining open to the public.

World.title: Foundation Provides Free Medical Outreach in Kwara, Targets over 3,000 Residents
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

As part of effort to take healthcare delivery to the people of the grassroots in Kwara State, a non governmental organisation, Eniobanke Foundation for Humanity has provided free medical outreach to over 3,000 residents of Ilorin on different kinds of ailments.

The outreach which commenced at Emir’s palace, Ilorin on Wednesday will come to an end on Friday at Tanke area of Ilorin, the state capital.

Speaking with newsmen in Ilorin on the sideline of the event held at Ilorin Emir’s palace, the Director of Programme of the foundation, Mr. Quadri AbdulSamad said that,

“Foundation is borne out of passion for service to

humanity and to give back to the society, with over 3,000 residents will be benefiting at the three days free medical outreach in Ilorin.

“It is also due to the foundation’s love for the people so as to boost their socio well being and to bring them closer to health care delivery and it is holding inconjuction with the Federal Medical Center, Markudi in Benue State.

“It is a free health outreach programme that would assist the residents of Ilorin to have access to free healthcare delivery without hindrance.

“The event will take three days and end at Tanke area of Ilorin with no fewer than 3, 000 residents of Ilorin having access to free medical service”.

Abdulsamad explained further that, the outreach was part of the mandate of the foundation to bring quality medical attention to the less privileged people in the society.

He said that, the outreach would assist the people suffering from different kinds of ailments to have access to medical attention from the qualified medical personnel recruited for the exercise.

AbdulSamad stated that, the exercise would also allow the medical personnel to embark on the testing of the beneficiaries and provide drugs free of charge to them while those that cannot be treated there would be referred to the appropriate medical centers.

He also said about seven states of the country, Kwara, Oyo, Ogun, Oyo, Edo, Cross River, Delta and Plateau would also benefit from the outreach is inconjuction with the Federal Medical Center, Markudi, Benue State.

Also speaking, the Medical Coordinator ot the outreach, Mr. Ibrahim Saddiq, said that, “We are basically to give back to the society through provision of free medical care to the beneficiaries.

“And we are going run test on HIV, High blood pressure, eyes, sugar among others..

“The beneficiaries would be allowed to see the Medical personnel recruited for the exercise.

“After the medical treatment, the beneficiaries would be provided with free drugs and those that are above the medical personnel would be referred to specialist hospital for proper attention”.

Most of the beneficiaries who spoke with newsmen lauded the humanitarian gestures of the foundation.

They said that the free medical outreach would reduce current burden of many households due to the present economic crunches in the country.

World.title: Don’t Stop Food Import Now, Fix Insecurity First, TUC tells FG
World.content:
*Seeks pay rise for workers

*Demands urgent passage of state police bill

Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The Trade Union Congress, (TUC) has urged the Federal Government not to suspend food importation, warning it will push up price of rice and other staples to unaffordable levels.

The union called on the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to consider revaluing the naira to N900-N1000 to a dollar, saying the current N1,380/$ rate is fuelling inflation and impacting negatively on workers’ earnings.

TUC however said it endorses government’s push for state police and the adoption of the NLNG privatization model for refineries.

TUC President-General, Comrade Festus Osifo, who spoke at a Press Conference in Abuja on Tuesday said that importation should continue until insecurity is tackled and farmers return to farms.

He used the opportunity to highlight the union’s position on the economy, security, labour, and governance issues

Responding to plans by the federal government to review the policy lifting of ban on importation of rice and other stable foods, TUC president said that the union is in support of sustaining food import untill such a time when food production improves with farmers having unfettered access to farmlands.

Osifo recalled that in early 2024, TUC submitted a 15-point demand to government, including measures to address food security.

He said insecurity had prevented farmers from accessing their farms, forcing prices up.

“At that time we told government to look for food all over the world, because it is when people see food to eat that they can go to work, that they can go to school,” he said.

He noted that the policy to grant licences for food importation helped to crash prices.

“We don’t want a bag of rice to go back to N100,000 or N120,000. Even where it is today, we still believe it is relatively high.,” he said.

The TUC leader said food importation should only be stopped “only and only if farmers can go back to farms” and the supply gap is closed. “When supply is limited and demand remains constant or increases, price is going to increase,” he said.

In addition, Osifo called on CBN to revalue the naira to N900-N1000 to a dollar, saying the current N1,380/$ rate is fuelling inflation without reflecting in workers’ wages.

Osifo also called on the Central Bank of Nigeria to revalue the naira to around N900 to N1000 to a dollar, arguing that the current rate of about N1,380/$ is still too high and is fuelling inflation.

He said while macroeconomic indicators have stabilised, “it has not dovetailed llllinto the microeconomy” where workers and traders feel the impact daily.

“The only people that devaluation helps is actually the workers, because every other item reflects the naira component. But what never reflects devaluation is the earnings of Nigerian workers,” he argued.

“We strongly believe that the fair value of our naira using purchasing power parity could be somewhere around 900 naira, maximum 1,000 naira to a dollar. CBN has what it takes to manage the exchange rate to about 1,000 naira,” he said.

TUC further said it endorses state police and the adoption of the NLNG privatization model for refineries.

He also said the union is in support of legalizing State Police, adding that the federal government should fast track the passage of Bill to help reduce insecurity in the country.

He dismissed fears of abuse of the state police by those in the helm of affairs at subnational, said that such concerns by few politicians should not negate its importance as a tool to address insecurity crisis across the country.

On refineries, TUC endorsed the NNPC plan to adopt the NLNG model — reduce government equity to 49% and bring in technical private investors with 51% — instead of outright sale.

The TUC commended the Director General of DSS , Oluwatosin Ajayi, for arrests and prosecution of bandits and terrorists.

He also hailed government’s salary increase of 50-80 percent for military personnel, saying that it should extend similar gesture to all public sector workers.

Regarding the ongoing strike by aviation workers, TUC said it supports the move by the affiliate union to get the management of airlines to allow their workers to unionize.

World.title: BBNaija S11: What ‘The Gambit’ Voting Reveals About Sentiment Over Strategy
World.content:
When Big Brother introduced “The Gambit” in the first week of Season 11, it gave viewers a rather unusual choice. One male and one female housemate would be guaranteed a place until the finale, but permanently barred from winning the ₦160 million grand prize. On paper, it was a strategic decision. Viewers could identify potential threats, protect housemates they felt were valuable to the show, or simply keep certain people around while taking away their shot at the money.

But what happened with the votes revealed something we already know too well: sometimes, Nigerians vote with their feelings first. Flora became the female Gambit with 29% of the votes, while Aikou took the male slot with 9%. And the two choices were interesting for different reasons.

Flora’s selection was driven largely by her appeal as a housemate. Viewers had already seen her boldness, energy and potential to bring drama, so for many, the thinking was simply: “She’ll make the show interesting, let’s keep her around.” Some may not have fully considered what making her a Gambit actually meant. As a Gambit, Flora was guaranteed a place until the finale but could no longer win the ₦160 million grand prize. So, in the end, the vote was less about making her the winner and more about wanting her to stay.

In other words, the appeal was not necessarily, “Flora should win.” It was more like, “I want Flora to still be here.” Here, sentiment did the one thing sentiment is supposed to do: it showed up as votes.

Aikou’s case complicates that picture. From the beginning, he had the “brains” thing going for him; calm, analytical, thoughtful and carrying that Professor-like energy. Certain viewers liked him for that; they saw someone intelligent and different from the usual loud personalities that often dominate reality television. But his numbers were also shaped by something closer to actual strategy: some viewers openly said they saw him as a threat and wanted him locked out of the prize while still in the house. That is a calculated move, not a sentimental one, and it sat alongside the viewers who just liked “the Professor” and wanted him around. Aikou’s vote, in other words, was a genuine mix of sentiment and strategy in a way Flora’s wasn’t.

Then came the first real eviction, and the picture flipped. Martins and Mercedes were the first to leave, with Martins receiving just 1.63% of the votes and Mercedes 2.29%, while Keivo narrowly survived with 2.92%.

Martins’ exit was fairly straightforward. A good number of viewers simply did not see enough of him. He was considered “low-impact” or “boring” by many, and there was not much emotional attachment pushing people to fight for his place in the house. Nobody was really making the argument that he had to stay because he was some dangerous strategic player.

Sometimes, you don’t get evicted because people actively dislike you. You get evicted because people don’t care enough to save you.

Mercedes was a completely different situation, and this is the case that actually reveals the gap. People clearly enjoyed Mercedes. Her energy, her boldness and her ability to create moments made her one of the more noticeable housemates. From the birthday lap dance for Martins to the arguments and her generally unfiltered personality, she was giving viewers something to talk about.

So when she left, the reaction was, understandably, “Wait, how?” People complained that one of the people actually bringing energy into the house had gone too soon. There was shock, frustration and the usual social media questioning of whether viewers were even voting properly.

But then you have to ask: if people really liked Mercedes that much, why didn’t enough of that liking translate into votes?

Many people loudly support housemates on social media without actually opening the MyDStv or MyGOtv app to vote. That small extra step can be the difference between a housemate who is widely loved online and one who actually receives enough votes to stay in the house. This is where Mercedes becomes the clearest evidence in the piece: not that Nigerians vote on feeling instead of strategy, but that feeling and voting are two separate acts, and a lot of us stop at the first one.

Flora shows sentiment successfully becoming votes. Mercedes shows sentiment failing to become votes. Put together, they suggest the real story isn’t “Nigerians vote with their hearts”, it’s that having a feeling about someone and being willing to act on it are not the same thing, and the size of that gap is what actually decides outcomes.

Most viewers are not sitting down to calculate who the biggest threat is, who should remain eligible for the ₦160 million grand prize or who will matter three weeks from now. Sometimes, the calculation is much simpler: “I like this person. I enjoy watching them. I want them to stay.” And to be honest, there is nothing strange about that. It is a reality show; people watch to be entertained, and emotional connection is part of what makes them care enough to vote.

That does not mean strategy is always better. Big Brother’s house run like a chess game would be boring. Personality, entertainment and emotional connection are part of what makes the show worth watching. The problem is when liking someone quietly substitutes for actually doing something about it, and we only recognise the gap after the fact.

The Gambit and the first eviction have offered a small but revealing mirror: what we feel about someone and what we are actually willing to do for them are not always the same thing. Perhaps the real question is not whether Nigerians vote with their hearts or their heads, but whether we notice the gap between feeling something and acting on it before the eviction, not after.

World.title: Terroso Moves to Strengthen Nigeria’s Cold Chain Infrastructure
World.content:
Iyke Bede

Terroso Agriculture, a subsidiary of Terroso Group, has joined the Global Cold Chain Alliance (GCCA), in a move aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s cold chain infrastructure and reducing post-harvest losses across the agricultural value chain.

The partnership will enable the company to leverage global expertise, industry standards, research and strategic partnerships in developing modern cold storage facilities, temperature-controlled logistics and preservation technologies.

Nigeria continues to lose a significant proportion of its agricultural produce due to inadequate cold chain infrastructure, which affects food security, farmer incomes, and the competitiveness of the agricultural sector.

Through its membership in the GCCA, Terroso Agriculture said it plans to support investments and partnerships that will improve the preservation and transportation of perishable agricultural products from farms to markets.

The GCCA represents companies involved in temperature-controlled warehousing, logistics and transportation globally, promoting practices aimed at preserving the quality and safety of perishable products while advancing innovation, operational efficiency and sustainability in cold chain operations.

Speaking on the development, Chief Executive Officer, Terroso Group, Opeoluwa Runsewe, said the partnership would support the company’s efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s food system through improved cold chain infrastructure.

“By working with GCCA, government and industry partners, we aim to reduce post-harvest losses, improve food security, strengthen supply chains, increase farmer incomes and build a technology-driven cold chain ecosystem that enhances Nigeria’s agricultural competitiveness and drives sustainable growth across Africa.”

Welcoming Terroso Group to the alliance, Manager, Marketing and Communications, GCCA, Serena Moriarty, said the company’s focus on cold chain infrastructure aligned with the organisation’s objective of strengthening temperature-controlled supply chains globally.

Senior Vice President, Global Market Engagement, GCCA, Adam Thocher, said the company’s focus on food preservation and supply chain infrastructure reflected the leadership needed to strengthen cold chain networks.

“We are excited to welcome Terroso Group into the GCCA community. Their vision for transforming food preservation and supply chain infrastructure reflects the kind of leadership required to strengthen global cold chain networks.”

Terroso Agriculture said it would continue to invest in cold chain infrastructure, logistics and agricultural value chains as part of efforts to improve food preservation, enhance supply chain efficiency and support long-term food security in Nigeria and across Africa.

World.title: UNICEF Seeks N1.2bn Nutrition Funding for Katsina
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has called on the Katsina State Government to increase its investment in child nutrition by allocating N1.2 billion to the Child Nutrition Fund in the 2027 budget.

The Chief of UNICEF Field Office, Kano, Mr. Shafeeq Ur-Rehman, made the request when he led a delegation on a courtesy visit to Katsina State Governor, Dikko Umaru Radda at the Government House weekend.

Ur-Rehman said the proposed N1.2 billion contribution by the state would be matched by UNICEF to strengthen interventions aimed at tackling malnutrition among children and women in the state.

He said the funding would support the procurement of Multiple Micronutrient Supplements for pregnant women, as well as Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) and other essential commodities for children under five suffering from severe wasting.

He commended the Radda administration for its consistent contribution to the Child Nutrition Fund, describing Katsina as one of the few states in Nigeria that had sustained its financial commitment to the fund over the years.

The UNICEF official stressed the need for increased investment in nutrition, particularly as the state continues to confront the challenge of child malnutrition.

He also disclosed that Katsina State was participating in a global pilot of the revised World Health Organisation (WHO) guidelines for the prevention and management of severe wasting in children.

Nigeria, he said, was one of only five countries selected globally for the pilot, which is currently being implemented in 10 local government areas of Katsina State.

Ur-Rehman said: “Katsina’s participation in this pilot is important because the lessons from here will not only contribute to nutrition programming in Nigeria but will also provide useful evidence for the global response to child malnutrition.”

He further commended Governor Radda for making Katsina the first and only state in Nigeria so far to appropriate N270 million for the implementation of a SMART Nutrition Survey.

He said the survey would generate reliable and timely nutrition data to identify vulnerable communities, guide resource allocation and strengthen interventions targeting women and children.

Ur-Rehman reaffirmed UNICEF’s readiness to support the state in conducting the Rapid SMART/SMART+ Nutrition Survey, stressing that evidence-based data remained critical to effectively addressing malnutrition.

Responding, Governor Radda pledged to include UNICEF’s additional N1.2 billion funding request in the state’s 2027 budget “despite the financial constraints facing the government”.

“We are not doing it for you; we are doing it for our people,” the governor said, assuring UNICEF of the state government’s continued commitment to interventions capable of producing measurable improvements in the lives of residents.

Radda said his administration had approved the release of N500 million as counterpart funding for the Child Nutrition Fund and described the investment as part of efforts to improve nutrition, healthcare and other development indicators in the state.

He said the collaboration between Katsina State and UNICEF had yielded encouraging results, particularly in the treatment of child malnutrition, adding that the number of children requiring treatment at stabilisation centres and outpatient treatment sites had begun to decline.

World.title: Eskom to implement a 13-hour power outage in Gauteng on Thursday
World.content:
Eskom has announced a major electricity supply interruption in the Cullinan area, affecting customers across several distribution lines. The power utility confirmed that Bigtree Moloto1 22kV customers with pole code BMM, Moloto 2 22kV customers with pole code 2BTM, and Sybrandskraal 22kV line customers with pole code BSK will all be affected.

The outage is scheduled for Thursday, 13 August, running from 7:00 to 20:00, a full 13 hours without electricity for the communities served by these lines. Eskom said the interruption is necessary to allow technical teams to conduct essential maintenance on the distribution network that keeps power flowing to homes and businesses in the region.

Safety warning issued to customers by Eskom

In its notice, Eskom urged residents to remain cautious throughout the outage period. The utility advised customers to treat all electrical appliances as live at all times during the power supply interruption, warning that power could be restored without prior notice once maintenance work is complete.



Eskom also included a disclaimer noting that circumstances beyond its control could affect the maintenance schedule. Should unforeseen issues arise, the planned work may not proceed as communicated, which could shift the restoration time. Also, the utility apologised in advance for any inconvenience the outage may cause to households, small businesses, and other customers who rely on a steady power supply.

Eskom has listed several channels customers can use to stay informed or report supply-related problems during the outage. These include the “MyEskom Customer” self-help app, available for download, and a WhatsApp line on 0860 037 566 for quick queries. Customers can also dial the USSD code *120*37566# for updates or access the Alfred chatbot through Eskom’s official chatroom link for automated assistance.

Additionally, for billing-related queries, the utility directs customers to its online portal, csonline.Eskom.co.za, available Monday to Friday between 8:00 and 16:00. Those needing to report supply issues directly can call Eskom’s Contact Centre on 08600 37566, which operates 24 hours a day.

The notice was developed by Eskom’s Gauteng Communication and Stakeholder Management team as part of its ongoing effort to keep customers informed about planned maintenance work across the province.

An Uber driver escaped injury after losing control of his vehicle and crashing into two parked cars outside the Taj Cape Town hotel. Image: Facebook @CapeTownCCID

An Uber driver escaped injury after losing control of his vehicle and crashing into two parked cars outside the Taj Cape Town hotel in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

The incident happened on Wale Street in Cape Town, when the driver reportedly lost control of the vehicle, crossed the median and smashed into two cars parked outside the hotel.

First responders

the Cape Town Central City Improvement District (CCID), its Safety and Security team was among the first responders at the scene.



Edward Edwardes, CCID Safety & Security night manager who was on duty at the time, said public safety officers immediately assisted and alerted the City of Cape Town’s Metro Police.

The Uber driver was not injured in the crash.

Provide assistance

The organisation also reported that its officers had responded to 16 motor vehicle accidents between 3 and 9 August, highlighting the frequency of road incidents in the central city.

The CCID said its public safety officers frequently act as first responders at accident scenes, providing assistance and contacting emergency services where necessary.

World.title: South Africa celebrates World Elephant Day
World.content:
South Africa is marking World Elephant Day by highlighting the importance of protecting the country's elephant populations. Image: Flickr

South Africa is marking World Elephant Day on Wednesday, 12 August by highlighting the importance of protecting the country’s elephant populations and strengthening efforts to promote coexistence between people and wildlife.

The Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) says the annual observance provides an opportunity to raise awareness about elephant conservation, habitat protection and the need to safeguard the species for future generations.

South Africa is home to an estimated 44 000 to 45 000 African savanna elephants, which form an important part of the country’s natural heritage, biodiversity, cultural identity and tourism economy.



The African savanna elephant is classified as Endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). Across Africa, elephants continue to face threats including habitat loss and fragmentation, as well as illegal killing.

National Elephant Heritage Strategy

South Africa reached an important milestone in its elephant conservation efforts earlier this year with the gazetting of the National Elephant Heritage Strategy (NEHS) on 29 May 2026.

Published under Government Gazette No. 54764, Notice No. 7545, the strategy provides a long-term framework for the conservation and sustainable management of elephants as a national heritage asset.



The NEHS promotes coordinated planning and cooperation between different levels of government and conservation authorities. It also emphasises regional connectivity and safe migration routes, particularly across Transfrontier Conservation Areas.

The strategy recognises that elephants have significance extending beyond conservation, with the animals contributing to South Africa’s ecological systems as well as its cultural and socio-economic landscape.

Protecting elephants while supporting communities

The department says successful elephant conservation will require cooperation between a wide range of stakeholders.



These include government institutions, conservation authorities, local communities, traditional leaders, the private sector, academic institutions and civil society organisations.

The approach is intended to strengthen partnerships and ensure that elephant conservation takes into account both environmental protection and the needs of communities living alongside wildlife.

On World Elephant Day, the department has reaffirmed its commitment to implementing the National Elephant Heritage Strategy and strengthening collaborative efforts to protect the country’s elephant populations.



With tens of thousands of elephants contributing to South Africa’s biodiversity and tourism economy, authorities say continued cooperation will be essential to ensure that their ecological, cultural and economic value is preserved for present and future generations.

World.title: The R100 grocery list that makes supper for a whole week
World.content:
In any other economy, you might be tempted to find a high-paying job to avoid the mid-month blues.

That may not be possible in this economy.

Instead, if you want your salary to last until month-end, you can rely on a trusty mid-month hack.



Spend R100 on this grocery list and get supper for an entire week.

R100 Buys a Grocery List that Makes Enough supper for a Week

This list can help you when funds are low. But it’s also scientifically proven to contain all the nutrients you need.

The three ingredients, when combined, should give you enough meals for the week.



Buy a starch. On a budget, you have two options: Maize meal and rice. Choose whichever suits your taste. This list relies on rice.

You can buy a 2-kilogram bag of parboiled long-grain white rice and have it cooked in 30 minutes.

Most weeks, supermarkets will have one brand of 2kg rice on promotion.



If your budget is strict, maize meal might be a better option.

It’s slightly more expensive to buy at R35 for 2.5kg, but you can get breakfast and supper from it.

Choose your protein. You really only have one option: pulses, also known as legumes.



Lentils will be the best choice because they’re key to the scientific process.

To get a tasty lentil dish, you need sauce. Stick to the rule: If you aren’t sneezing, it’s not seasoned.

Use any meaty marinade in your fridge or meat-flavoured spice in your cupboard.



With enough meaty flavour, you won’t get any earthy notes common when cooking lentils.

Choose your vegetable. To create a complete dietary profile, choose butternut or carrots.

Butternut offers you the most value for money.

You can get a pocket weighing roughly 6 kilograms for R40.



Carrots, on the other hand, cost R20 for 1 kilogram.

You can also buy an onion, one or two tomatoes, and some green pepper to flavour your lentils, should you make any savings.

If you fill a bowl with 50% rice, 25% lentils and 25% butternut, you should be able to get 21 meals from these ingredients.



You could comfortably feed two people supper with this list.

But families may need to get a second bag of lentils to last for a week of suppers.

Item Price Whole Lentils 500g R28 Butternut Pocket R40 Rice R32 Total R100



Where to Splurge

If you have more than R100 and want some actual meat in the meal, you have two options: chicken soup packs or pork.

Chicken soup packs are sold at Pick ‘n Pay and Shoprite for R55 per kilogram.

Pork sells for R60 per kilogram at most supermarkets.



The Science Behind the Complete Meal

Beyond being affordable, this meal is scientifically proven to contain every nutrient you need.

According to a daily nutritional calculator, the average South African* should be getting the following nutrients:

Nutrient Requirement One Plate of R100 Supper Protein 26 g 4.3 g Fibre 25 g 11 g Vitamin A 700 μg 488 μg Vitamin B6 1.3 mg 0.5 mg Vitamin C 45 mg 14 mg Iron 18 mg 4.3 mg Magnesium 310 mg 77 mg Potassium 2 800 mg 631 mg Zinc 8 mg 2.1 mg

*The average South African is based on data from Statistics South Africa.



A 350-gram bowl of lentils, rice, and butternut can get you roughly 25% of these nutrient requirements.

This is based on Eat This Much: cooked and unsalted rice (175g), lentils (87.5g), and butternut (87.5g).

There are also other health benefits to this cost-effective meal.



Data from ScienceDirect shows that lentils are good for your gut and help with digestion and inflammation. Butternut can help lower or control cholesterol.

Now, should you fall on hard times, you know what to buy with only R100.

World.title: This week’s snowfall was epic, but doesn’t match ‘Snowtember’
World.content:
This week's Eastern Cape snow warning was serious, but South Africa's real snow record dates back to September 2024: Image ChatGPT

This week’s Orange Level 6 warning cut off parts of the Eastern Cape and made for genuinely dramatic headlines.

But is it an Eastern Cape snow record?

No.



South Africa’s real benchmark for severe snow dates back to September 2024. This week doesn’t come close.

What actually happened this week

SAWS issued an Orange Level 6 disruptive snow warning for the Eastern Cape’s Emalahleni, Sakhisizwe, Senqu, Elundini and Matatiele municipalities, warning of major traffic disruption and communities becoming temporarily inaccessible.

It was serious enough that a SAWS forecaster later confirmed the system itself, while significant, “was not out of the ordinary” for a South African winter.

The Eastern Cape snow record actually belongs to September 2024

In September 2024, a system nicknamed “Snowtember” triggered a SAWS Level 8 warning. It shut the N3 Toll Route completely between Estcourt in KwaZulu-Natal and Harrismith in the Free State for close to two days.

Motorists were stranded for more than 14 hours in freezing conditions, with reports of at least one death linked to exposure.

Five provinces were affected, including the Eastern Cape, and it took a full multi-agency rescue and recovery operation to clear stranded vehicles from Van Reenen’s Pass.



Why this Eastern Cape snow record comparison matters

It’s easy for a dramatic week to feel like “the worst we’ve seen,” especially when it’s playing out in your own backyard. But stacking this week’s system against 2024’s shows just how much more severe South African winters can get.

I think it’s worth remembering these events when they happen, because it puts each new cold front into real perspective rather than just headline shock value. Hey, I for one wish I got the opportunity to see the snow in 2024.

World.title: Transfer news: Pirates links swirl as Polokwane coach speaks on Matuludi
World.content:
Polokwane City coach Willy Moloto has addressed the absence of star defender Thabang Matuludi from the matchday squad amid continued transfer speculation.

The 26-year-old right-back has attracted interest from several top clubs, including Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns, in recent months. He was heavily linked with a move away from Polokwane City during the current transfer window.

However, Moloto insists Matuludi’s absence has nothing to do with the ongoing speculation surrounding his future.



“There’s no such thing. Every time people don’t see a player, they start with the talk,” Moloto told FARPost.

The Polokwane coach explained that Matuludi has been dealing with minor knocks after being involved with Bafana Bafana at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

“Remember, Matuludi was also with Bafana Bafana [at the 2026 FIFA World Cup], and he picked up some knocks in training.

“The team has also been doing well, so sometimes there is no need to change.”

Matuludi sidelined but…

“If it’s not broken, why fix it? He will get his chance—there are a lot of games.

“Let’s give the youngster [Surprise Manthosi] a chance. He did well even though he had some mistakes in the first half [in the league tie against Stellenbosch on Tuesday],” he said.



Despite Moloto playing down concerns over Matuludi’s absence, the defender continues to be linked with a move to one of the country’s biggest clubs.

Orlando Pirates are reportedly among the favourites to secure his services, particularly after the Buccaneers released two right-backs in July.
