World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.title: Assam floods: Toll rises to 103; 87,000 remain affected in four districts
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The flood situation in

showed signs of improvement on Wednesday, with the number of people affected falling to around 87,000 across four districts. However, the death toll from this year's floods rose to 103 after two more people died in the past 24 hours.

The latest figures from the Assam State Disaster Management Authority showed that one person drowned in Sivasagar and another in Karbi Anglong.

Around 86,800 people are still affected by the floods in Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Sivasagar. Golaghat remains the worst-hit district, with more than 42,000 people affected. Nagaon has around 20,000 affected residents, while Sivasagar has about 15,000.

The situation has nevertheless improved compared with Tuesday, when nearly 1.13 lakh people were affected across the four districts.

Authorities are continuing relief operations in the affected areas. A total of 79 relief camps and distribution centres are currently operating across five districts, providing assistance to 13,011 people.

Over the past 24 hours, relief agencies distributed nearly 96.55 quintals of rice, 18.26 quintals of dal, 5.41 quintals of salt and more than 204 litres of mustard oil among flood-affected families.

Despite the improvement, the floods continue to damage homes, farmland and infrastructure.





According to ASDMA, 433 villages remain underwater, while more than 10,884 hectares of crop land have been damaged across the state.

Floodwaters have also damaged embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure in several districts.

The Dhansiri River at Numaligarh continues to flow above the danger mark, adding to concerns in the affected areas.

The floods have also affected livestock. More than 32,900 domestic animals and poultry have been impacted across Assam.

While the overall number of people affected has declined, the rising death toll and continuing damage to villages, farmland and infrastructure show that the flood crisis is far from over.

World.title: China says India border 'generally stable' amid tensions in Arunachal

China said the India-China border remains âgenerally stableâ while sidestepping reports of increased Chinese military activity near Arunachal Pradesh.

China said Wednesday that the situation along the India-China border was âgenerally stable at the momentâ, while declining to confirm reports of increased Chinese military activity in disputed areas near Arunachal Pradesh.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a regular press briefing in Beijing in response to questions about videos circulating on Indian social media that purportedly showed heightened Chinese military activity along the border.Guo said China and India had held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on Border Affairs the previous week. He said both sides had agreed to maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels and work together to preserve peace and tranquillity along the border.The comments came a day after India reiterated that its border with China remained a matter of serious concern and that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control was essential to the broader relationship between the two countries.The Chinese response also came amid reports of heightened military activity by Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradeshâs Upper Subansiri region. Beijing claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of what it calls âSouth Tibetâ, a claim consistently rejected by New Delhi.India had separately pushed back against Chinaâs objections to New Delhi formally identifying 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard Indian names. The Ministry of External Affairs said the state was an âinalienable and integralâ part of India and that nothing could change that reality.The latest exchanges come as India and China continue efforts to stabilise ties that deteriorated sharply after the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes and a prolonged military standoff along the border.The two countries reached a disengagement agreement covering the remaining friction points at Depsang and Demchok in October 2024.Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping subsequently held talks in Kazan, followed by further diplomatic efforts aimed at improving bilateral relations.

World.title: 'Has no shame': Kangana Ranaut attacks Rahul Gandhi over Amit Shah debate row, Parliament logjam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP MP

on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition

over the continuing stalemate in Parliament, accusing him of making a "mockery" of the House and the country while refusing the government's offer for a debate on the students' protest.

Ranaut alleged that Gandhi was demanding a statement from Union home minister

over the police action against protesters, while simultaneously saying the opposition would not listen to him.

"I feel he is making a mockery of the country. He constantly ridicules the nation; for him, everything is a joke. This is the first time I am seeing Parliament being made such a mockery of. In the same breath, he says, 'We want an answer from Amit Shah ji--asking whether or not he did such-and-such to the students--while simultaneously declaring, 'We are not here to listen to him'.

He has no sense of shame or propriety left," news agency ANI quoted Ranaut saying.

"The whole world is watching and wondering what kind of person this is. The way he is venting his frustration and insulting Parliament and, by extension, the entire nation and its citizens convinces me, as someone observing his role as leader of the opposition, that this will be his final term," she added.

Ranaut, who represents Mandi in the Lok Sabha, also attacked Gandhi over his political record, saying the Congress under his leadership had "lost a hundred elections" and claiming that he would not retain the leader of opposition post in the future.





"He is demanding the resignation of the Prime Minister--a democratically elected leader who has secured a massive mandate for a third consecutive term. He seems to think that no one else in this country should even exist but him. Then there are his other actions--colluding with figures like Soros or international forces to tear the country apart and leave it in ruins. Ultimately, it doesn't matter whose resignation he demands or what he wants, because the public simply doesn't care about him," she said.

World.title: Cybersecurity at nuclear installations accorded highest priority; AERB, external govt agencies assess security at plants: Centre
World.content:
Chennai: The Union govt on Wednesday informed Lok Sabha that security assessments are conducted periodically at all nuclear power plant sites by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) and âexternal govt agencies.

â

In a written reply to Congress MP Manickam Tagore, minister of state in the Prime Ministerâs Office Jitendra Singh said the plants also conduct internal security assessments. âThe observations made are reviewed, monitored and necessary upgrades are carried out for compliance,â he said.

Tagore had sought details of third-party security audits at nuclear plants, including Kudankulam, and measures to counter threats from drones, cyberattacks and sabotage.

He asked whether any foreign or suspected state-sponsored cyberattack attempts had been detected during the past three years.

The National Alliance of Anti-nuclear Movements urged the Union govt recently to constitute a commission of inquiry to investigate the alleged leak of files related to the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant. The statement comes in the wake of a ransomware group reportedly publishing hundreds of files linked to the Kudankulam plant which are said to be highly sensitive.





The govt did not directly disclose whether any such foreign or state-sponsored attempts had been detected. It said cybersecurity at nuclear installations was accorded the âhighest priorityâ, with continuous monitoring and surveillance mechanisms in place. Preventive measures include access controls, regular security audits, vulnerability assessments, incident-response mechanisms and capacity-building programmes.

It cited CERT-inâs (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) role in issuing alerts and advisories, coordinating responses to cyber incidents and operating the National Cyber Coordination Centre.

On physical security, Singh said nuclear power plants were equipped with perimeter intrusion-detection systems, access controls, CCTV surveillance and X-ray baggage inspection facilities. The AERB conducts regulatory inspections covering nuclear security.

Singh said regulatory-approved emergency preparedness plans were in place at every nuclear power plant, including Kudankulam. Exercises involving local administration, security agencies and plant authorities are conducted periodically, and feedback is used to revise and strengthen preparedness plans.

An ICCR exercise was conducted at the Kudankulam nuclear power plant on April 15, 2025.

The govt said all other nuclear power plant sites had conducted their latest ICCR exercises since Sept 2024. At Kalpakkam, an off-site emergency exercise involving the district administration, was conducted on July 17, 2026, with an initiating event from the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor.

World.title: 'Got firebombed by Indians on net': Trump aide Navarro recalls backlash after Russian oil, tariff remarks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: US senior counsellor for trade and manufacturing Peter Navarro has said President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have a âvery good working relationshipâ and will resolve differences over the US tariff issue linked to Indiaâs imports of Russian oil.

Responding to an ANI question, Navarro recalled the backlash he faced in India after writing an op-ed on the India-Russia oil trade.

âDuring the Ukraine-Russia war, 6-8 months ago, I think I wrote an op-ed, which absolutely factually correctly pointed out that prior to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, India was not involved in the oil trade with Russia, but afterwards it got heavily involved and was selling a lot of refined products on behalf of Russia, which helped feed the war machine,â Navarro said.

âAnd that issue has been resolved. Maybe I had a little bit to do with that with that op-ed, but I can tell you, I got actually firebombed by the Indian continent on the internet. All I would say to you, don't do that,â he added.

Navarro, however, said the issue would ultimately be handled by Trump and Modi themselves.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âThat's not how we resolve problems here in America. With respect to your question, the President and your Prime Minister have a very good working relationship.





They are going to work that out amongst themselves, and it's not for me or any gaggle to get between that,â he said.

His remarks come amid renewed concerns in India over possible US trade measures targeting countries that continue to purchase Russian energy.

Earlier on August 7, the US Senate passed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by an 86-11 vote. The bipartisan legislation would give the US president discretionary authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from countries that are among the top five buyers of Russian crude oil or natural gas.

India and China remain among the largest buyers of Russian crude.

World.title: ED arrests ex-treasurer of Cong's Chhattisgarh unit in Rs 3,000 cr liquor scam

Chhattisgarh Congress leader Ramgopal Agrawal (Photo: Agencies)

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate has arrested Ramgopal Agarwal, former treasurer of the Congress in Chhattisgarh, in an ongoing money laundering investigation in the Rs 3,000 crore liquor scam in the state. The agency said a substantial part of the proceeds of crime, generated in cash, was delivered to Agrawal in his capacity as the then Treasurer of the Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress Committee.Agrawal, who was lodged as an undertrial in the Central Jail, Raipur, was arrested on Tuesday and has been remanded to ED custody for seven days. He is accused of criminal conspiracy, cheating, forgery and corruption in the excise administration of Chhattisgarh during 2019 to 2023.âInvestigation revealed that a syndicate comprising Anil Tuteja (retd IAS), Anwar Dhebar and Arun Pati Tripathi (an Indian Telecom Service officer) orchestrated a large-scale scam in the stateâs liquor trade and generated proceeds of crime of Rs 3,000 crore through illegal commission on liquor sales, unaccounted country liquor sale, commission collected from distillers and from foreign liquor companies and against the grant of FL-10A licences,â ED said.The agency further said that âstatements recorded of the persons who handled and moved the cash have revealed that the cash was delivered, at the instance of Ramgopal Agrawal and through handlers of the syndicate, at Rajiv Bhawan, Raipur, the then office of the Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress Committeeâ.Agarwal was summoned for questioning earlier, and in his statement subsequently recorded, he gave evasive replies, the agency said.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Panel indicts ex-judge in cash case; LS deadlock continues over debate on students' protest & more
World.content:
Lok Sabha panel indicted ex-judge Varma over unaccounted cash found at his residence.

found at his residence. Amit Shah offered a 24-hour debate on alleged student protest crackdown; Rahul Gandhi rejected it.

Tata Sons chairman Chandrasekaran resigned after differences with Tata Trusts over reappointment.

Kiren Rijiju defended FCRA Bill as opposition criticised it as anti-minority.

Iran reportedly knew Trump's location during NATO summit, prompting Secret Service to use decoy aircraft.

Here are top 5 stories of the day

Lok Sabha inquiry panel indicts ex-HC judge Yashwant Varma in cash-at-home case

A Lok Sabha inquiry committee indicted former Allahabad high court judge Yashwant Varma in the cash-at-home case, finding his explanation for the discovery of unaccounted cash at his official residence "evasive" and "unsatisfactory.

" The panel said all three charges against Varma â possession of unexplained cash, failure to preserve evidence, and furnishing misleading explanations â were proved. Varma resigned during the inquiry.

Amit Shah offers to answer all questions; Rahul Gandhi says 'not interested in lecture'

Union home minister Amit Shah offered to sit in Parliament from "3pm today till 3pm the next day" to respond to opposition concerns over alleged police action against student protesters, but leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi rejected the offer, saying the opposition seeks answers, not lectures.

Shah said the government was ready for a detailed discussion, while Rahul demanded answers on who ordered the use of force against students.

Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran steps down, to serve out term till February

Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran resigned, saying he would not offer himself for reappointment when his term ends on February 20, 2027, and asked the board to begin the succession process soon. The decision comes after differences with Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata over the group's future governance, including a board deadlock over his extension.

'India not banana republic': Rijiju defends FCRA Bill amid opposition criticism

Union minister Kiren Rijiju strongly criticised the opposition over what he called a "misleading campaign" against the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, saying India is not a "banana republic" and there must be rules to regulate foreign funds. Iran knew Trump's hotel floor, targeted his aircraft during Nato summit: Report

Iranian operatives knew which floor of Donald Trump's hotel in Ankara he was staying on and posed a specific surface-to-air missile threat to his aircraft during the Nato summit, prompting an elaborate security deception in which the president was secretly moved out of Turkey inside a catering container while a decoy Air Force One flew with top officials aboard, according to a New York Times report. Trump later secretly rejoined the aircraft before disembarking in front of cameras.

World.title: SJM calls for boycott of US brands over tariff threat
World.content:
RSS-affiliated Swadeshi Jagran Manch has called for a boycott of American products

NEW DELHI: From Russian oil to Pepsi, Coke and social media, the Swadeshi Jagaran Manch has sought to turn the latest US tariff threat into a wider âswadeshiâ campaign, calling on Indians to boycott American products and platforms and asking the Centre to stay firm in trade negotiations with Washington.The RSS-affiliated economic body reacted to legislation passed by the US Senate that, according to SJM, would empower the American President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries making significant purchases of Russian oil. It said the move amounted to an attempt to dictate Indiaâs energy choices.âNo country has the right to dictate Indiaâs energy security and sovereign trade policy,â SJM national co-convenor Ashwani Mahajan said, adding that Indiaâs Russian crude purchases were driven by price, availability, supply diversification and consumer interests.SJM said the proposed measure assumed greater significance with India and the US engaged in negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement, arguing that talks âcannot be conducted on gun pointâ.It also urged the Centre to reconsider two recent policy moves which it claimed favoured US companies â changes allowing FDI e-commerce entities greater flexibility over inventory for exports and an amendment enabling merchant discount rate on certain UPI transactions.Going further, SJM called for a ban on US tech and social media companies if Washington pursued what it termed âunilateral economic coercionâ. It asked citizens to begin by boycotting Pepsi, Coke and US-owned social media and e-commerce platforms, saying the campaign could be expanded if American actions continued.The organisation asked the government to reject any attempt to link tariffs with Indiaâs oil purchases and not compromise on agriculture, dairy, energy security or strategic autonomy during trade negotiations.SJM maintained that access to the US market should not be used to force third countries to alter their energy sourcing decisions.

World.title: Training programme for traditional artisans held
World.content:
Around 110 beneficiaries under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme attended a training programme aimed at enhancing their technical skills, knowledge for market access, and entrepreneur capabilities. It was held at the District Industries Centre here recently.

Organised by the MSME Development and Facilitation Office, Chennai, in coordination with Puducherry District Administration, the training programme saw participation by traditional artisans who are working as doll/toy makers, goldsmiths, sculptors, cobblers, and basket/coir weavers in Puducherry.

An official release, here, said the programme was aimed at improving business opportunities and enhancing the livelihood of traditional artisans. Speakers explained various benefits being extended by the Central government under the PM Vishwakarma scheme to the artisans. The programme featured a series of technical sessions aimed at enhancing the capacity and market readiness of the beneficiaries under the scheme.

The Indian Institute of Packaging, Chennai, conducted a session on product packaging, labelling and design, highlighting their importance in marketing of products. Members from the Export Promotion Council Hub, Bengaluru, gave lectures on opportunities and avenues for accessing international market.

There was also a session on Artificial Intelligence along with facilitation for the onboarding of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries on Udyam Registration Portal, thereby promoting digital adoption and formalisation among artisans and craftspeople, the release said.

K. Dhayalan, Joint Director and Head of Office, MSME, DFO office Chennai, Jayaraman, General Manager, District Industries Centre, Puducherry and Preetika Sharma, Assistant Director, MSME-DFO, spoke at the inaugural session, the release added.

World.title: Chalavadi Narayanaswamy objects to appointment of the Registrar (Evaluation) of the University of Mysore
World.content:
Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council, Chalavadi T. Narayanaswamy, who has accused B.K. Kempegowda of being illegally appointed as the Registrar (Evaluation) of the University of Mysore, has urged the government to immediately cancel the appointment. He has written to the Chief Secretary and the Secretary, Higher Education Department, demanding that a senior professor of the university be appointed to the post of Registrar.

The government had issued an order on August 10, 2026, appointing Prof. Kempegowda as the Registrar (Evaluation) of the University of Mysore.

“Regarding the post of Registrar (Evaluation) of Mysore University, there is a rule that the appointment should be made from among professors or senior faculty members working in universities affiliated to the Higher Education Department,” the letter reads.

“The rules do not permit the appointment of professors working under the Department of Collegiate Education or the Department of Technical Education to this post. However, the appointment of Prof. Kempegowda, who is working as a professor at the Government First Grade College, Nanjangud, to the post of Registrar (Evaluation) is against government rules and the spirit of the Karnataka State Universities Act,” he stated.

Mr. Narayanaswamy further alleged that there were allegations of sexual harassment and misuse of grants against Prof. Kempegowda.

Reacting to the allegations, Prof. Kempegowda said, “The State government has already appointed professors from private colleges and Government First Grade Colleges to the posts of Vice-Chancellor and Registrar in several universities. My appointment has also been made in the same manner. Apart from this, there is no substance in the allegations of sexual harassment and misuse of SC/ST funds against me. If the Chief Secretary and the Secretary of the Higher Education Department issue a notice in this regard, I will provide clarification with the necessary documents.”

World.title: Opposition ‘fled’ from meaningful debate in Monsoon Session, says BJP chief
World.content:
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nitin Nabin on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) accused the Congress and other Opposition parties of avoiding parliamentary debate and disrupting the Monsoon Session, alleging that they were “neither serious nor earnest” about issues concerning the people.

“Parliament is the sacred temple of democracy where the direction of the country is determined through meaningful discussions on the people’s issues, but in this Monsoon Session, the irresponsible Congress fled from discussions and repeatedly shifted its goalposts, thereby tearing apart the democratic decorum and dignity of the country,” he said on X.

Mr. Nabin said: “In reality, Congress has betrayed the people of the country. Throughout this entire session, the conduct of Rahul Gandhi and the entire opposition exposes their anarchic mindset and anti-democratic thinking. The whole session is nearly over, yet they were not ready for a serious discussion on even a single issue.”

The BJP chief said first, the Congress demanded a discussion on youth issues, and when the government was fully prepared for it, the party and its allies “backed out, claiming they did not want any discussion at all”.

Stating that it was the first session for many new MPs, Mr. Nabin said the Opposition “presented an utterly shameful picture” of Indian democracy before them by “creating chaos”. He accused Mr. Gandhi of bringing “disgrace” to the position of Leader of the Opposition through repeated use of “indecent language, arrogance, flip-flopping, and irresponsible attitude”.

Mr. Nabin said the Opposition parties “were fleeing from discussions” because they feared that their “lies” would be exposed when the Union Home Minister spoke in Parliament. “Out of this very fear, the Opposition kept changing topics throughout the session and running away from discussions,” he said.

World.title: Govt revises ACC PLI timelines for Ola Electric; unlocks up to ₹7,240 crore
World.content:
Ola Electric Mobility Ltd. on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) said the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has approved revised timelines under the ACC production-linked incentive scheme for Ola Cell Technologies Pvt Ltd (OCT), its wholly owned subsidiary.

The MHI revision is much more than a timeline extension. The approval secures a full five-year PLI window through CY2031 for Ola Electric's 20 GWh allocation and unlocks up to ₹7,240 crore in cumulative PLI incentives, the company said in a statement.

Disbursements will be made quarterly, beginning next quarter, creating a recurring incentive stream as Ola Electric scales its cell business, it added.

Ola Electric currently has 2.5 GWh of installed cell-manufacturing capacity, with a further 3.5 GWh under installation.

The company will reach 6 GWh by the end of the current quarter, achieving the initial installed-capacity milestone well ahead of the revised December 2026 timeline.

The MHI decision has effectively extended the original timelines by two years. Lithium cells are becoming a foundational technology across electric mobility, energy storage, drones, robotics and next-generation industrial systems, Ola Electric said.

Building these capabilities in India will strengthen the country's energy security and technology independence while creating a globally competitive domestic battery ecosystem, it added.

Ola Electric is building a multi-chemistry cell platform spanning NMC and LFP technologies, supported by indigenous R&D, increased localisation of battery materials, improved manufacturing yield, and closed-loop material recovery.

Bhavish Aggarwal, Chairman and Managing Director, Ola Electric, said: "The revised timeline is more than an extension. It transforms the economics of our cell business by converting an earlier milestone overhang into a five-year, quarterly PLI opportunity of up to ₹7,240 crore." He further said, "We hadn't factored any incentives into our business projections after overshooting the original timelines. Ola is now well ahead of the government's revised schedule, and enables us to access the full potential of ₹7,240 crore and receive disbursement as soon as next quarter." At the company's annual Sankalp event on this Independence Day, Ola Electric will unveil its broader energy product roadmap-including Shakti, Mahashakti, and the next phase of its energy platform.

World.title: PU organises research conclave
World.content:
Vice Chancellor of Pondicherry University P. Prakash Babu has stressed the need to inculcate the spirit of research among students.

Participating at the Research Conclave 2026 organised by the University, the Vice Chancellor said institutions should organise more programmes to nurture a strong research temperament among students in the country. Scholars and students should go beyond academic publications in the field of research, he said.

He emphasised the importance of patenting, technology transfer, and commercialisation. Efforts should be made to translate the research outcomes for betterment of society and economic upliftment, a release from PU said.

Research scholars from various disciplines, including Arts, Science, Humanities, Engineering and Management presented their findings at the conclave. The conclave was an opportunity to showcase the research activities undertaken by the University, the release added.

World.title: Karnataka Bandh unlikely to disrupt normal life as most organisations extend only moral support
World.content:
Normal life is unlikely to be affected on Thursday (August 13) despite the bandh call given by Kannada activist Vatal Nagaraj against the directive to release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, as most organisations have extended only moral support to the call.

The bandh, scheduled from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., is unlikely to affect public or private transport, shops and commercial establishments, hotels or eateries. Schools and offices are also expected to function as usual. Essential services such as healthcare, grocery stores, pharmacies and banks are expected to remain functional. Transport services are also likely to operate normally, as autorickshaw and cab unions have extended only moral support to the bandh.

On Wednesday, Mr. Nagaraj said that the Kannada Okkoota had decided to go ahead with the bandh and that he would not call it off. He also said they would carry out a rally from Town Hall to Freedom Park at 11 a.m.

“From 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., the bandh will be effective. Mandya will be entirely shut down, and complete support will be received in Hubballi, Dharwad, Raichur and Ballari,” he said.

While Mr. Nagaraj had initially said that the bandh in the State was in protest against the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) directive to release water to Tamil Nadu, he clarified on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) that the bandh was also intended to highlight all major irrigation and development issues, including the Kalasa-Banduri and Mekedatu projects.

As a precursor to the event, Mr. Nagaraj’s group held a demonstration with “brooms” at Majestic Bus Stand on August 12 before being escorted away by the police.

Meanwhile, Kannada outfit Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (KRV), which has been at the forefront of several protests in the state, has said that it is not extending support to the bandh. Dinesh Kumar, organising secretary of KRV, said the bandh would not solve the issue, but a legal battle would, which the government was pursuing.

Rudramurthy of the Auto Rickshaw Drivers’ Union and Tanveer Pasha of OTU both told The Hindu said they were only extending moral support to the bandh, as stopping operations would disrupt the lives of lakhs of people.

Emphasising that they support the State’s lawful efforts to secure Karnataka’s rightful share of water for drinking and irrigation purposes, K. Radhakrishna Holla, president of the Karnataka State Travel Operators Association, said they were not extending support to the bandh, but only moral support to the cause.

“Our transport, tourism and service sectors are directly connected with the daily needs of the public. In an internationally recognised city like Bengaluru, continuity of transport, tourism, hospitality, business and other essential services is extremely important,” he said.

Educational institutions to remain open

Meanwhile, private schools, including those affiliated with the Karnataka Associated Management of Schools (KAMS), have withdrawn their earlier advisory regarding the closure of schools in connection with the ‘Cauvery Bandh’, citing the loss of academic days.

“As a symbolic gesture of solidarity, school management representatives, teaching staff and non-teaching staff may wear a black ribbon or black strip on the day of the bandh without disrupting academic activities,” said D. Shashikumar, general secretary, KAMS.

P.C. Rao of the Bruhat Bengaluru Hotels Association also said that the association was extending only moral support, citing food as an essential service.

Box

Police warn against bandh

Bengaluru police have warned against forced shutdowns and road blockades. In a statement, the police said several organisations had called for the bandh, while others had informed the Bengaluru City Police that they were not supporting it. The police said citizens have the democratic and fundamental right to express their views and hold peaceful protests within the framework of the law. However, they stressed that the rights of those who do not wish to participate must also be respected.

“No individual or organisation should force, threaten or compel anyone to participate in the bandh,” the police said, warning against the forced closure of shops, establishments and institutions, obstruction of traffic, and compelling people to participate in protests against their will.

Precautionary security arrangements have been made across Bengaluru, with adequate police deployment, patrolling and security measures at important and sensitive locations.

World.title: Mallikarjun Mansur Kala Bhavan to be opened for public soon: Bellad
World.content:
Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly Arvind Bellad on Wednesday said that renovation work of Dr. Mallikarjun Mansur Kala Bhavan in Dharwad would be completed and made available for public use soon.

Speaking to press persons after inspecting the ongoing renovation works at the kala bhavan, Mr. Bellad said that the renovation was being undertaken at a cost of ₹1.50 crore from the MLA’s grant and ₹1 crore from the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation, he said, adding that the facility would be opened for public use immediately after work completion.

He said that the renovated kala bhavan would be available for music, theatre and other cultural activities.

“The renovation will be carried out in accordance with the requirements of artists and writers. Their views will be taken into consideration before taking a final decision on the facilities to be provided,” he said.

Mr. Bellad also said that the Kadapa Maidan in front of the kala bhavan was being renovated for public use. The ground, located in the heart of the city, had hosted several historical meetings and programmes attended by prominent personalities from Karnataka and across the country. It would be restored and made available for public activities, he said.

Municipal councillor Suresh Bedre, along with several leaders and officials, was present during the inspection.

Meeting

Earlier, Mr. Bellad took part in a meeting with the coordinators of “Save Kala Bhavan and Kadapa Maidan Committee” at Karnatak Vidyavardhak Sangha and took their suggestions.

Vocalist Pt. Venkatesh Kumar, scholar Viranna Rajur, general secretary of Sangha Shankar Halagatti and several other personalities spoke on the occasion, and urged him to ensure that auditorium and the ground were made available for public use at the earliest.

World.title: Independence Day 2026: How MBS Youth Choir in Kerala is upholding patriotic fervour through choral music
World.content:
‘Thikkugal ettum sithari, Pakka malaigal udainthu, Andam saayuthu’... It was a goosebump-worthy moment when members of MBS Youth Choir (MBSYC) sang the lines from Subramania Bharathi’s poem, ‘Mazhai’, with vigour and power in their voices. The poem captures the all-consuming fury of nature – heavy downpour, thunderstorm, winds, lightning and the destruction that ensues. But, on a deeper level, the poet was calling for massive, public uprising against the British.

It is one among the hundreds of songs set to tune by MB Sreenivasan or MBS, who believed that music has the power to bring in change. As the nation enters the 80th year of independence, MBSYC is not only holding fast to the legacy of MBS, who pioneered a tradition combining Indian classical and folk tradition with Western harmony, but also his objective to promote secularism, peace and unity through music.

“We are the only choir in Kerala that follows this format of singing, without break for the last 38 years,” says Ashok S, coordinator of the choir, which was an initiative of his father, late Subramania Sharma or Sharmaji. While Ashok and his sister Anitha S are the coordinators, another sibling S Santhi is the patron of the choir formed in 1988, after the passing of MBS by Sharmaji and a group of like-minded musicians and prominent figures in the cultural circle of Thiruvananthapuram.

The choir meets every Saturday at Lenin Balavadi, Vazhuthacaud, for rehearsals. “Times have changed. But what drives us is the energy we get from the songs and the dedication of the singers. Over the years, probably 1,000 singers have come and gone. Right from composer M Jayachandran, who trained under MBS and was there during the formation of the choir. He still acknowledges the role played by the choir in his musical journey,” Ashok adds.

John Mathai, 61, secretary of the choir and one of its founding members, adds that they were actually fulfilling MBS’ dream with the launch of the group. “MBS had once said that Thiruvananthapuram should have a choir. So when we got together for the condolence meeting after his sudden demise, Sharmaji recalled his wish,” says John.

The new choir soon came under the wings of Madras Youth Choir (now known as Madras MBS Choir), which was started by MBS in 1971. “Since then, every year, trainers from the choir come down to Thiruvananthapuram to teach us new songs. MBS was particular that human voices should have prominence and not the instruments. So we stick to just tabla and harmonium in our songs and at times add keyboard or guitar,” he says.

The choir currently has four conductors — Gokul VB, Sreedevi Narayanan, S Sreekumar and VS Ramachandran. Sreekumar and Ramachandran train the children’s choir also. Members who have been part of the choir from the beginning are Jayanthi B, Uma Vijayachandran (vice president), Dhanalekshmi Premjith and Ashalatha AR. B Vinod Kumar is the president.

The patriotic song repertoire has songs in over a dozen regional languages, most of them written by reputed poets. This include songs in Malayalam (‘Janmakarini’, ‘Ethu videsathu’, ‘Kezhuka priya naade’), Tamil (‘Thikkukual’, ‘Anumathiyon’, ‘Paarukkulle nalla naadu’), Hindi (‘Hind desh ke nivasi’, ‘Ye waqt ki’), Kannada (‘Cheluvina mudina’, ‘Ee mannu namudu’), Marathi (‘Aata uthau’, ‘Bharatamatha’), Assamese (‘Ei matire’), and Odia (‘Ae desha ae maati’). Among the poets who wrote the verses are P Bhaskaran, Vallathol, and ONV Kurup from Malayalam, besides those from other languages, such as Pandit Vinayachandra Maudgalya, RN Jayagopal, Sane Guruji, Sathish Das, Prem Dhawan, and Niranjan Rout.

Looking back at the journey of the choir, the senior members recall how Sharmaji put forward a suggestion to teach patriotic songs to school children in the golden jubilee year of Indian independence in 1997. Members of the choir travelled across the State to train children to perform on Independence Day at respective district headquarters. “The songs were ‘Vande Mataram’, ‘Saare jahan se achcha’ and ‘Bharatha samudayam’,” says Ashok.

At present, membership is open for those in the age group of 15 to 40. They have to audition to be part of the choir. Among the members are working professionals, homemakers, youngsters and school/college students.

At a time when the patriotic fervour of the Gen Z and Gen Alpha is being questioned, the choir has quite a few members in that age group. Bhava Priya, pursuing her post-graduation at University of Kerala, Karyavattom campus, says, “I get goosebumps every time I sing a patriotic song. I feel overwhelmed, especially while singing ‘Thikkugal’, ‘Jayabheri’, ’Aata uthau’ etc,” she says.

It is a rule that the singers have to learn all songs by heart and are not allowed to use the choirbook. “When the trainers teach us, they explain the meaning of the song as well. Thus we get more connected to the song,” John adds.

Becoming a member was an eye-opener for Kalyani PN, a Plus Two student of Cotton Hill Girls HSS, who joined around a month ago. “I didn’t know that we had so many patriotic songs until I joined the choir. There is a special feeling when I render them. My favourite is the Sanskrit song ‘Samarasa bhavana Bharata samrajyam’. I hope to continue to be part of the choir.”
